== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L13
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L86-L172
    86  /// and the single-lane phase B.
    87  const USAGE: &str = "\
    88  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>]
    89                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
    90                 [--] FILE.ndjson
    91         con-ron [flags] --olean --search-path=DIR[:DIR...]
    92                 [--constant=NAME]... [--] MODULE...
    93         con-ron --help
    94  
    95    (C), the Rust arena checker of con-ron's DESIGN.md section 8: con-leche's
    96    pure checker over an append-only DAG of per-constructor handle arrays, with
    97    con-leche's command line and con-leche's exit codes, so that
    98    scripts/diff-e2e.sh can run the same 383 fixtures against this binary and
    99    the Lean twin `con-ron-lean` alike.  A term is a u32 handle into a Vec: on
   100    the checking path there is no Arc, no tagged pointer and no reference count
   101    at all.  (The PINNED DATA the checker compares against is still
   102    con-leche's own constants as Expr values, interned into the persistent tier
   103    once at startup -- crates/con-ron-core/src/lib.rs says why.)
   104  
   105    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   106                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   107                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists), so a stream
   108                      declaring a theorem of type False is never accepted.  The
   109                      same two statements are PROVED about this program's
   110                      pipeline (ConRon.Capstone.model_exists and
   111                      no_False_declaration, on the Aeneas model of the Rust),
   112                      using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and
   113                      Quot.sound.  What they still assume are hypotheses, not
   114                      axioms: that the driver runs the extracted stages in the
   115                      order it does on the file's bytes.  They hold at every pin
   116                      text and every prelude.  OVERVIEW.md section 3.1 lists
   117                      them.
   118    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   119                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   120                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   121    --jobs=<n>        the check phase runs on <n> worker threads sharing the
   122                      persistent tier and the installed index by reference
   123                      (DESIGN.md section 8.3): each worker owns a scratch tier,
   124                      its own caches and a copy of the pin handles, and the
   125                      results are merged by record index and walked in record
   126                      order, so the verdict and the record a rejection names are
   127                      the same at every <n>.  Default: one per hardware thread,
   128                      capped at 16.  A worker reserves 1 GiB of stack, which a
   129                      `ulimit -v` must allow for.  0 or a non-numeral is a usage
   130                      error, as in con-leche.
   131    --                every argument after it is a file, whatever it is called;
   132                      FILE.ndjson is a regular file, read forward (a FIFO or a
   133                      directory is exit 3)
   134    --olean           read the input from .olean files instead of a lean4export
   135                      stream: the arguments are root modules (Init, Std, Mathlib,
   136                      ...; a component in «» is taken literally), checked with
   137                      every constant of their import closure.  The closure is
   138                      read at the private level (theorems with proofs,
   139                      definitions with bodies), merged as Lean's own import
   140                      merges it, and emitted as the records lean4export would
   141                      write, so the same checker checks them.  Every object the
   142                      imports and constants reach is decoded and validated,
   143                      nothing in the files is trusted.  A file of another .olean
   144                      format version declines (2).  OVERVIEW.md says how far the
   145                      theorems reach on this path.
   146    --constant=NAME   with --olean: check only this constant and what it
   147                      mentions, not every constant of the closure, as
   148                      lean4export's arguments after -- do; a component of digits
   149                      is a number (_private.M.0.foo).  May be given more than
   150                      once.  A name the closure does not hold is an error (3).
   151    --search-path=DIR[:DIR...]
   152                      the directories holding .olean trees, as LEAN_PATH lists
   153                      them (the toolchain's lib/lean, a package's
   154                      .lake/build/lib/lean).  May be given more than once.  Every
   155                      module is looked up in every directory: its files (M.olean
   156                      and, for a module of the module system, exactly
   157                      M.olean.server and M.olean.private beside it) must be in
   158                      one directory, counted once however often it is reached (a
   159                      repeated entry, a symbolic link).  A module in two places,
   160                      a missing, stray or split part is an error (3).
   161  
   162  build-time selection (cargo features, not command-line flags): the global
   163  allocator is `con-ron-dump`'s `#[global_allocator]`, chosen on this crate's
   164  dependency edge -- `cargo build --release` is mimalloc, `--no-default-features`
   165  is glibc `malloc`, and `--no-default-features --features jemalloc` is jemalloc.
   166  It is the same edge `crates/con-ron` has, so the two checkers are measured on
   167  the same allocator unless a build says otherwise.
   168  
   169  Any other option is a usage error: the run reports it, prints this text and
   170  exits 3 without reading its input.
   171  
   172  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.

    19  //! |---|---|---|
    20  //! | 0 | `accepted N declarations` | every declaration checked; `N` counts the file's declaration records |

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L18-L137
    18  /-!
    19  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    20  
    21  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    22  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    23  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    24  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's two headline theorems in the shape
    25  the original campaign used (`conron.model_exists` /
    26  `conron.no_False_declaration`, `proof/ConRon/RefineOld/Main.lean`):
    27  
    28  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — every environment the Aeneas model of the
    29    Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    30  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    31    type `False` is never accepted by it.
    32  
    33  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    34  frontier is measured as the dependency closure of these two, and it is
    35  EMPTY since `arena` `db1131f1` (task #97-MILESTONE): both depend on
    36  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` only (§5's census).  What they
    37  still assume is exactly their premises, listed below.
    38  
    39  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    40  
    41  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    42  around six extracted core functions and the pin decoder, in this order, on
    43  one `AState` made from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    44  
    45      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    46        → prepare_prelude → (decode) → intern_all_pins → (the declaration fold)
    47  
    48  The headlines (§4) take one premise per call, from the binary's own start
    49  values `startState`/`emptyTier` (§3); §4's table maps each premise to its line
    50  of `check_main`.
    51  
    52  and the twin runs the same six stages (`Arena/Main.lean`'s
    53  `runPipelineHead`/`runPipelineTail` drive them for `con-ron-lean`).  **The sixth stage is the fold the
    54  binary's driver runs, pool and all** (task #97-P5-POOL):
    55  `driver::check_decls_driver` runs phase A with the heartbeat as its hook,
    56  freezes the tier, runs phase B on `pool::parallel_all`, and thaws the tier.
    57  The headlines take one premise per step (`h6` phase A, `hord` the jobs' order, `h7` the
    58  freeze, `hlayer` the value checks' layer, `h8` phase B), which `poolAccepts_intro` assembles
    59  into `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  Phase B's premise `h8` is the contract
    60  of the generic combinator `pool::parallel_all` with the driver's two verified closures
    61  (`ParallelAll` at `jobStep`): index lists, one per worker, covering every job, and for each
    62  a fold of `run_job` over its indices from `worker_state`, accepting.  That contract is the
    63  pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.
    64  The theorems hold for EVERY install hook, so they cover the plain run and
    65  `--progress` alike.  `pool_accepts_refines` relates the stage to the twin's
    66  `Arena.PooledAccepts`, and `Bridge/Checker/Phased.lean`'s
    67  `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` carries that to the pure fold.  So the
    68  statement takes the six Rust RUNS as premises (that the binary's
    69  `check_main` makes exactly these calls, in this order, is the one trusted
    70  line, exactly as it was for the original campaign), and the proof is:
    71  
    72  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s six `…_refines` lemmas walk the
    73     Rust runs into six TWIN runs from the twin's own start state
    74     `AState.init EStore.empty`, related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/
    75     `AStateInv`: lockstep);
    76  2. **Theorem 1** — the twin runs feed `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`, whose
    77     pure fold accepts the denoted stream: con-leche's
    78     `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` gives the model, and
    79     `no_False_theorem_accepted_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream
    80     (`stages_no_False`, through the pure fold);
    81  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a
    82     model.
    83  
    84  Every step is an existing theorem; what this file adds is glue: the Rust
    85  runs threaded through `Sim₀`/`SimStream`/`SimFold`, and the one twin-store
    86  fact the composition needs from Theorem 1 — `StoreWF` at the headline's
    87  `AStateRel` (`stages_storeWF`) — read off its stage lemmas.  Theorem 2 itself
    88  carries no fact about the twin's store (task #97-T2-AUDIT).
    89  
    90  ## The named hypotheses
    91  
    92  Since task #98-HEADLINE the headlines start from the binary's own start
    93  values (`startState` = `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`)
    94  instead of quantifying over a start state with `hpers`/`hest`/`hst0`
    95  equations, name the call the binary makes at each step (`prepare_d`, not
    96  `prepare_prelude`).  Beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape
    97  `hfalse` and the one premise per call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`, `hord`, `hlayer`), what
    98  they assume is exactly:
    99  
   100  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks
   101    (task #97-P5-Driver): the binary parses with the verified reader loop
   102    `parse_source` over the driver's file handle, and
   103    `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that
   104    `parse_chunks` over the chunks the handle hands out; that the handle hands
   105    out the file's bytes, in order, is the input seam — the one seam left.
   106  
   107  Former hypotheses, now theorems or gone (DESIGN.md's task #97-COMPOSE and
   108  #98-HEADLINE sections tag each with its owning lane):
   109  
   110  * ~~`InitRel`~~ — the Rust start state is related to the twin's: a theorem
   111    since task #97-P5-Top (`Refine2/Checker/Init.lean`'s `init_rel`);
   112  * ~~`hk : CoreSpec Arena.checkFuel`~~ — Theorem 1's Core tier
   113    spec: a theorem since task #97-P3-Core round 6
   114    (`Bridge/Checker/Hyp.lean`'s `CoreSpec.of_core`);
   115  * ~~`hind : IndSpec`~~ — Theorem 1's inductive tier spec:
   116    `Bridge/Inductives/Decl.lean`'s `indSpec_of_bridge` since task #97-P3-Ind
   117    round 8 (the stage lemmas below still take it as a parameter);
   118  * ~~`hbytes`~~ — the prelude's bytes are con-leche's: not needed since task
   119    #98-HEADLINE.  con-leche's `preparePrelude` puts the prelude's records into
   120    the checked stream, so soundness holds whatever the prelude parses to
   121    (`Bridge/Frontend/Prepare.lean`'s `builtinPreludeE_run` is parametric in
   122    the bytes).  The gate `scripts/gen-prelude-lean.sh --check` stays, as the
   123    claim that con-ron ships con-leche's prelude;
   124  * ~~`hsc : ScanSpec`~~ — Theorem 2's scanner seam: a theorem since task
   125    #97-P5-Front (`Refine2/Frontend/Scan/Spec.lean`'s `scanSpec`);
   126  * ~~`hpers`, `hest`, `hst0`~~ — the start state and tier were universally
   127    quantified with three equations; since task #98-HEADLINE they are the
   128    constants `startState`/`emptyTier` (`startState_eq`);
   129  * `hdec` is now `hpins`, the premise for the binary's pin step: the pin list
   130    is what the verified decoder read, at any text (as con-leche's theorems
   131    hold at every pin list); `model_exists_embedded` /
   132    `no_False_declaration_embedded` fix the text to the embedded `PINS_TEXT`;
   133  -/

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L826-L830
   826  def RustDenotes (fe : arena.env.IFEnv) (st : arena.monad.AState)
   827      (env : ConLeche.Env) : Prop :=

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L339-L358
   339      }
   340  }
   341  
   342  /// con-leche: none — a frontend failure's exit, one place: the decline, the
   343  /// reject and the internal error of the two frontend gates and of the
   344  /// preparation (con-leche writes the three arms out at each gate).
   345  fn frontend_exit(e: &CheckError, mode_tag: &str) -> u8 {
   346      match classify(e) {
   347          FrontendClass::Declined(what) => {
   348              eprintln!("con-ron: declined: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   349              2
   350          }
   351          FrontendClass::Invalid(what) => {
   352              eprintln!("con-ron: invalid: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   353              1
   354          }
   355          FrontendClass::Internal(msg) => {
   356              eprintln!("con-ron: {} ({})", msg, mode_tag);
   357              3
   358          }

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean#L34-L38
    34  def ReadsAs {S : Type} (inst : frontend.export_c.ChunkSource S) :
    35      S → List (alloc.vec.Vec Std.U8) → Prop
    36    | src, [] => ∃ e src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (e, src') ∧ e.val = []
    37    | src, c :: cs => c.val ≠ [] ∧
    38        ∃ src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (c, src') ∧ ReadsAs inst src' cs

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L575-L587
   575  structure SnapshotOf {Fs : Type} (inst : frontend.olean.files.OleanFs Fs) (fsv : Fs)
   576      (F : ConLeche.FS) : Prop where
   577    path_exists : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.path_exists fsv p = ok (.Ok b) →
   578      b = (F.real q).isSome
   579    real_path : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ r, inst.real_path fsv p = ok (.Ok r) →
   580      F.real q = some ⟨ConRon.Refine.absString r⟩ ∧ ConRon.Refine.StrWF r
   581    read_bin_file : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.read_bin_file fsv p = ok (.Ok b) →
   582      F.file q = some (absBytes (alloc.vec.Vec.deref b))
   583    read_range : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ off len b, inst.read_range fsv p off len = ok (.Ok b) →
   584      ∃ whole, F.file q = some whole ∧ absBytes (alloc.vec.Vec.deref b) =
   585        whole.extract off.val (min (off.val + len.val) whole.size)
   586    file_size : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ s, inst.file_size fsv p = ok (.Ok s) →
   587      ∃ whole, F.file q = some whole ∧ s.val = whole.size

   315      /// which is what makes a premature read a stop rather than a wrong
   316      /// answer (task #97c's hazard).

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L30
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```
    14  //!
    15  //! (tier 0 = persistent, 1 = scratch; the index is into THAT CONSTRUCTOR'S
    16  //! array of THAT TIER).  The zero word is a narrow handle — tag 0,
    17  //! persistent, slot 0 — which is the twin's `default : Idx k` and every
    18  //! `of_word(0)` below: the anonymous name, the level `zero`, a handle that
    19  //! decodes.  An expression `app` array holds 2^30 = 1 073 741 824 nodes per
    20  //! tier and every other constructor array 2^26 =
    21  //! 67 108 864: apps are 85 % of an export's expression nodes, so they are the
    22  //! array that runs out first, and they get the room.  Only the expression
    23  //! `app` tag is wide — a level `param` handle is narrow although `LTAG_PARAM`
    24  //! has `ETAG_APP`'s value — and `word_tag` reads `ETAG_APP` off a word with
    25  //! bit 30 set, so the tag of a handle is read the same way for all four
    26  //! kinds.
    27  //!
    28  //! The tier is the TOP bit, above both shapes' index, so a persistent
    29  //! handle's bits never change when the scratch tier comes and goes
    30  //! (con-leche's lesson 6).

  3631      /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:482-502 EStore.intern
  3632      /// Hash-cons an expression node: probe the persistent cons table, then the
  3633      /// scratch one, then append to the tier the store is in (DESIGN.md §8.3).
  3634      /// The cap test is the Lean's `capOK` turned into the `Native` decline
  3635      /// §8.3 puts here.
  3636      ///
  3637      /// **Dispatched ONCE** (task #97-P6-15).  The body below used to run the
  3638      /// whole sequence over the `ENodeView`, and each of its four steps
  3639      /// dispatched on the view's tag again and built the node record again:
  3640      /// the persistent probe built it (inside `ETables::find`), the scratch
  3641      /// probe built it a second time, `der_of_view` re-dispatched to compute
  3642      /// the derived word, and `ETables::push` re-dispatched and built it a
  3643      /// third time to append it.  So the tag is read once here and the ten per-constructor
  3644      /// paths below each build their record ONCE and hand the same `&r` to the
  3645      /// two probes, to the capacity test and to the push — the same clauses in
  3646      /// the same order, with the dispatch and the two rebuilds gone.
  3647      ///
  3648      /// The twin's `intern` is one `def` over `ENodeView`; what is owed is the
  3649      /// ten-arm spelling and `internC v = intern (view of C)` per constructor,
  3650      /// each of them `rfl` after the `match`.
  3651      pub fn intern(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, v: ENodeView) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3652          match v {
  3653              ENodeView::BVar(i) => self.intern_bvar(pers, i),
  3654              ENodeView::FVar(idx, ty) => self.intern_fvar(pers, idx, ty),
  3655              ENodeView::Sort(u) => self.intern_sort(pers, u),
  3656              ENodeView::Const(n, us) => self.intern_const(pers, n, us),
  3657              ENodeView::App(f, a) => self.intern_app(pers, f, a),
  3658              ENodeView::Lam(ty, body) => self.intern_lam(pers, ty, body),
  3659              ENodeView::ForallE(ty, body) => self.intern_forall_e(pers, ty, body),
  3660              ENodeView::LetE(ty, val, body) => self.intern_let_e(pers, ty, val, body),
  3661              ENodeView::Lit(l) => self.intern_lit(pers, l),
  3662              ENodeView::Proj(n, i, e) => self.intern_proj(pers, n, i, e),
  3663          }
  3664      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L3915-L3962
  3915      pub fn intern_app(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, f: EIdx, a: EIdx) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3916          let r: AppNode = AppNode { f, a };
  3917          let sk: bool = if self.scratch_on {
  3918              if r.f.is_persistent() {
  3919                  !r.a.is_persistent()
  3920              } else {
  3921                  true
  3922              }
  3923          } else {
  3924              false
  3925          };
  3926          let hit: Option<EIdx> = if sk {
  3927              None
  3928          } else if pers.frozen {
  3929              pers.e.apps.find(&r)
  3930          } else {
  3931              self.pers.apps.find(&r)
  3932          };
  3933          match hit {
  3934              Some(hp) => Ok(hp),
  3935              None => {
  3936                  if self.scratch_on {
  3937                      let at: (usize, Option<EIdx>) = self.scr.apps.find_slot(&r);
  3938                      match at.1 {
  3939                          Some(hs) => Ok(hs),
  3940                          None => {
  3941                              if self.scr.apps.full_wide() {
  3942                                  Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3943                              } else {
  3944                                  let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3945                                  let h: EIdx =
  3946                                      EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_S, self.scr.apps.size() as u32);
  3947                                  self.scr.apps.push_at(at.0, r, d, h.dup2());
  3948                                  Ok(h)
  3949                              }
  3950                          }
  3951                      }
  3952                  } else if self.pers.apps.full_wide() {
  3953                      Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3954                  } else {
  3955                      let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3956                      let h: EIdx = EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_P, self.pers.apps.size() as u32);
  3957                      self.pers.apps.push(r, d, h.dup2());
  3958                      Ok(h)
  3959                  }
  3960              }
  3961          }
  3962      }

 10427  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/StateC.lean:336-343 CState.flushed
 10428  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3693-3699 flushCaches` — **what
 10429  /// the per-declaration bracket does to the caches**: it drops them whole,
 10430  /// which is con-leche's own `flushC`, the operation its driver runs at exactly
 10431  /// this point.
 10432  ///
 10433  /// Task #97-P4c ported DESIGN.md §8.3's survivor policy instead — keep the
 10434  /// rows whose key AND value are persistent — which is sound and strictly more
 10435  /// caching; task #97f measured what it costs (`filter` is `O(table)` and the
 10436  /// survivors accumulate, so the fold pays `O(declarations × surviving rows)`:
 10437  /// 16 % of `Init`'s first 4 380 declarations' cycles, 213 s → 124 s).  The
 10438  /// twin's `Caches.dropScratchEntries` stays as the SPECIFICATION of a
 10439  /// surviving row, and so does `Caches::drop_scratch_entries` below it with
 10440  /// its eleven journals — P3 needs it to state that flushing is sound.
 10441  pub fn flush_caches(st: &mut AState) {
 10442      st.caches.reset();
 10443  }
 10444  
 10445  /// con-leche: none — **the per-declaration bracket, closed** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 10446  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3701-3709 dropScratch` — drop the
 10447  /// scratch tier of the store and the cache entries that name it, in one
 10448  /// operation, so the two halves cannot drift apart; and **thaw** the store:
 10449  /// the tier `enter_scratch` handed out comes back (task #98-FREEZE), so the
 10450  /// store is owned and scratch-off again.
 10451  pub fn drop_scratch(st: &mut AState, tier: PersTier) {
 10452      flush_caches(st);
 10453      st.store.thaw(tier);
 10454  }
 10455  
 10456  /// con-leche: none — **the per-declaration bracket, opened** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 10457  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3711-3718 enterScratch` — turn the
 10458  /// scratch tier on, and clear the per-call memo tables of `Memos`, which
 10459  /// belong to no tier and whose keys the new tier may reuse.  **Opening a
 10460  /// bracket is freezing the store** (task #98-FREEZE): its persistent tables
 10461  /// are handed back as the `PersTier` every read inside the bracket goes
 10462  /// through and promotion writes, and every append inside it is a scratch
 10463  /// append.
 10464  pub fn enter_scratch(st: &mut AState) -> PersTier {
 10465      st.memos.reset();
 10466      st.store.freeze()
 10467  }

     1  //! `arena::promote` — the scratch → persistent copy (DESIGN.md §8.3, task #97-P6-2).
     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Promote.lean`, declaration for
     4  //! declaration, under DESIGN.md §8.6's lockstep ruling.
     5  //!
     6  //! DESIGN.md §8.3, "**Phase A runs in the scratch tier too, with promotion**":
     7  //!
     8  //! > The install phase (annotate the type and the value, infer, defeq) was
     9  //! > interning every intermediate into the persistent tier — on `Init` 5.06 M
    10  //! > permanent nodes on top of the parse's 6.14 M (+82 %) […].  The arena's
    11  //! > answer is con-leche #64's: phase A opens the scratch tier like phase B,
    12  //! > and the two handles it must keep (the annotated type, the annotated
    13  //! > value) are **promoted** — a memoised structural copy scratch →
    14  //! > persistent […] before the tier is dropped.  Persistent handles are
    15  //! > promoted to themselves.
    16  //!
    17  //! This module is that copy, at all four handle kinds and lifted to
    18  //! `arena::env`'s declaration layer, plus `promote_new` — the entry
    19  //! `arena::checker`'s two fold steps call, which promotes a step's NEWLY
    20  //! INSTALLED constants in place.
    21  //!
    22  //! ## What it is
    23  //!
    24  //! `view` the node, promote its children, `intern` the result into the
    25  //! PERSISTENT tier (`arena::store`'s `intern_persistent` family, whose section
    26  //! note carries the WF obligations).  Three properties make it cheap and make
    27  //! it right:
    28  //!
    29  //! * **a persistent handle promotes to itself**, by one tier-bit test
    30  //!   (`is_persistent`) and one decode, so that a handle reaching the persistent
    31  //!   tier is one it can read.  Most of what a step
    32  //!   leaves behind IS the parsed term (since task #119 a value kind's record
    33  //!   is exactly the parsed one), so the walk stops at the first persistent
    34  //!   node on every branch;
    35  //! * **the memo makes it `O(result)`** and not `O(unfolding)`: the subject is
    36  //!   a hash-consed DAG, and an unmemoised structural copy of a DAG is the
    37  //!   mistake task #97g's item 5 found three times over.  The memo is per
    38  //!   DECLARATION — a scratch handle means nothing once the tier is dropped —
    39  //!   and it is threaded as an argument-and-result pair, a moved
    40  //!   `ron::HashMap` returned, which is `frontend::proj_rec`'s spelling for its

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L998-L1020
   998  /// con-leche: none — the phase boundary, which con-leche has no tier to make
   999  /// Lean twin: none — the twin has no tier to move; its phase-B worker reads the
  1000  /// persistent tier where it is (`AState.worker`, `Arena/Checker.lean`).
  1001  /// **The persistent tier and the installed index out of phase A and into a
  1002  /// value**: the four persistent tables and `fe` move into one `PersTier` handed
  1003  /// back `frozen`, for the phase-B workers to read (`fe` is what `ifenv_find` reads
  1004  /// below an own layer).  A pure MOVE: the store's scratch tiers and flags are
  1005  /// untouched (a worker's store is its own, `worker_state`), and `thaw_tier` puts
  1006  /// everything back where it was.  The driver's store is not read between the two.
  1007  pub fn freeze_tier(ar: &mut EStore, fe: IFEnv) -> PersTier {
  1008      let n: NTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.ns.pers, NTables::empty());
  1009      let l: LTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.pers, LTables::empty());
  1010      let ls: LsTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.pers, LsTables::empty());
  1011      let e: ETables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.pers, ETables::empty());
  1012      PersTier {
  1013          frozen: true,
  1014          n,
  1015          l,
  1016          ls,
  1017          e,
  1018          env: fe,
  1019      }
  1020  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L1211-L1263
  1211  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:365-373 EStore
  1212  /// **The persistent tier of all four stores, as one value `n` phase-B workers
  1213  /// read by reference** — DESIGN.md §8.3's "the persistent tier is immutable in
  1214  /// phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — no atomics anywhere", made
  1215  /// expressible.
  1216  ///
  1217  /// Each store keeps its own `pers` field, which is the tier the PARSE and
  1218  /// phase A's setup append to, and ONE flag, `scratch_on`.  **A store is in
  1219  /// one of two states, and "frozen" and "scratch on" are the same thing** (task
  1220  /// #98-FREEZE):
  1221  ///
  1222  /// * **owned, scratch off** (the parse, the setup, between phase A's
  1223  ///   declaration brackets): read through the EMPTY stand-in tier
  1224  ///   (`PersTier::empty`, `frozen` false), so every persistent read and every
  1225  ///   append goes to the owned field;
  1226  /// * **frozen, scratch on** (inside a declaration bracket, and a phase-B
  1227  ///   worker for its whole life): the owned field is empty — `freeze` moved it
  1228  ///   into a `PersTier` whose `frozen` bit is set — and the store is read
  1229  ///   through that tier, so every persistent read goes to it; every append is
  1230  ///   a SCRATCH append, so no append can reach a frozen persistent tier, by
  1231  ///   construction and not by a guard.
  1232  ///
  1233  /// Which tables a persistent read goes to is therefore the READER's to say
  1234  /// (`frozen`), not the store's: the choice is made by a value that is fixed
  1235  /// for the whole of a bracket or a worker, whatever runs inside it.  `freeze`
  1236  /// hands out a frozen tier and turns the scratch tier on; `thaw` takes it back
  1237  /// and turns it off; `empty_frozen` is a worker's store.  Promotion — the one
  1238  /// writer of the persistent tier inside a bracket — writes the frozen tier
  1239  /// itself, through `&mut PersTier` (`PersTier::intern_*`).
  1240  ///
  1241  /// **Why a shared PARAMETER and not a field of the state.**  Task #97-P6-6
  1242  /// measured a region inside the threaded `&mut` state eight ways: a bare
  1243  /// `&u64` field on `AState` costs five function bodies Aeneas cannot
  1244  /// translate and the same borrow inside the four stores costs sixteen, while
  1245  /// everything else this split needs — the two-tier layout, the flag, the
  1246  /// value-returning readers below — extracts at zero errors.  So the sharing
  1247  /// arrives as an ordinary shared parameter, the shape `fe: &IFEnv` and `mode:
  1248  /// &CheckMode` already have, and the twin's monad becomes `ReaderT PersTier
  1249  /// (StateT AState (Except CheckError))`.
  1250  pub struct PersTier {
  1251      /// This is a frozen store's tier: a store read through it reads its
  1252      /// persistent tables HERE.  `false` only for the empty stand-in an owned
  1253      /// store is handed (`PersTier::empty`), which is never read.
  1254      pub frozen: bool,
  1255      pub n: NTables,
  1256      pub l: LTables,
  1257      pub ls: LsTables,
  1258      pub e: ETables,
  1259      /// The installed environment's frozen base (`arena::env`'s `IFEnv` note):
  1260      /// `checker::freeze_tier` moves phase A's index here, so every phase-B
  1261      /// worker reads one by reference.  An empty layer in every other tier.
  1262      pub env: IFEnv,
  1263  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/env.rs#L618-L673
   618  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/FEnv.lean:98-136 FEnv
   619  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Env.lean:225-234 IFEnv` — the environment
   620  /// with its `O(1)` index (DESIGN.md §8.3 lesson 13).  Entries with counter
   621  /// `< visible_below` are visible; `visible_below` doubles as the next counter
   622  /// `push` hands out.  con-leche's `ovl` field is not ported (see `ifenv_find`).
   623  ///
   624  /// **The environment has two tiers, like the store.**  An `IFEnv` is one
   625  /// LAYER: phase A threads one by value and pushes into it; `freeze_tier` moves
   626  /// it into the `PersTier`, where it is the frozen BASE every phase-B worker
   627  /// reads by reference; and a phase-B job's `fe` is a layer of its own over that
   628  /// base, empty until the job pushes (`ifenv_layer`).  `ifenv_find` and the
   629  /// table lookups read the own layer first, then the base below `base_below`:
   630  /// con-leche's worker view (`FEnv.base`, whose entries are visible below
   631  /// `FBase.below`), with the frozen tier as the base.
   632  ///
   633  /// **The READERS take the bound as a scalar** (`vis: u64`, task #97-P6-6b),
   634  /// and this field is what phase A — which threads the record by value and
   635  /// pushes into it — passes them.  Phase B passes `pc.vis` and never touches
   636  /// the record, which is what lets `n` workers share one `&IFEnv`.
   637  ///
   638  /// **The index row is `(counter, SLOT)` and not `(counter, IConstantInfo)`**
   639  /// (task #97-P6-5, lever 1).  The twin's row carries the constant itself,
   640  /// which in Lean is a shared value; in Rust it was a SECOND full copy of
   641  /// every stored constant — `env.consts[s]` and `idx[name].1` held the same
   642  /// record twice, both of them deep — and `ifenv_dup` therefore copied the
   643  /// environment twice, each copy a `Vec<NIdx>` malloc per constant.  The
   644  /// Mathlib profile of task #97-P6-5 put that at **19 % of the whole run**
   645  /// (72 % of the install phase), because `arena::inductives` copies the
   646  /// environment three times per inductive block and Mathlib has 6 720 of them
   647  /// over a 691 128-entry environment.
   648  ///
   649  /// The row is now the constant's SLOT in `env.consts`, so the map is a POD
   650  /// and `dup` is a slot memcpy.  Every writer keeps the two in step —
   651  /// `ifenv_push` pushes then indexes, `promote::index_promoted` writes the
   652  /// slot back and re-indexes it, `promote::erase_installed` only removes — and
   653  /// `ifenv_find` reads `env.consts[s]`.  The refinement relation for `IFEnv`
   654  /// says `idx[n] = (c, s) ∧ consts[s] = ci` where the twin says
   655  /// `idx[n] = (c, ci)`; no twin clause moves and `find?` answers the same
   656  /// constant (task #97-P6-5's twin ledger).
   657  ///
   658  /// **The table map `tbls` is built the same way, for the same reason**: its
   659  /// row is the table's slot in `env.tables`, where the twin's (con-leche's
   660  /// `Std.HashMap Name ProjTable`) is the table.  It has no counter: a table is
   661  /// visible exactly where its structure is (`ifenv_find_table`), so the prefix
   662  /// views — phase B's `pc.vis` — need nothing of their own for it.
   663  pub struct IFEnv {
   664      pub env: IEnv,
   665      pub idx: HashMap<NIdx, (u64, u64)>,
   666      pub visible_below: u64,
   667      pub tbls: HashMap<NIdx, u64>,
   668      /// The frozen base's entries are visible to this layer below this counter
   669      /// and no further (con-leche's `FBase.below`): a block job's position, the
   670      /// largest counter for a value check's layer, `0` for phase A's own, which
   671      /// has no base.
   672      pub base_below: u64,
   673  }

   173  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/ExprOps.lean:54-56 Inst1MemoInv
   174  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:63-107 Memos` — the memo tables of
   175  /// the `ExprOps` twins, in one record.
   176  ///
   177  /// con-leche threads each memo as an explicit argument-and-result pair

   179  /// `con_ron_core::kernel::expr_ops` turns that into a `&mut HashMap`
   180  /// parameter; the arena carries the eight tables in the state instead, which

   182  ///

   184  /// NEST: `instantiate1Lift`'s `bvar` arm runs `liftLooseBVars`, so a shared
   185  /// table would answer one walk with the other's answers.  One of those walks
   186  /// has no cursor (`instLPGo` keys on the node alone); the arena keys it at

   191  pub struct Memos {

   200      /// `instantiate1Lift` (`ExprOps.lean:2222-2261`).

   206      /// `fvarRange` (`ExprOps.lean:1397-1422`).
   207      pub fvar_b_c: HashMap<EIdx, u64>,
   208      /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-P6-13)
   209      /// **The level substitution at a LEVEL handle**, for `instLPGo`'s `.sort`
   210      /// arm: `ks` and `us` are fixed for the whole `instLPFast` call, so the

   212      /// top-level call, so the substitution vector is not in the key".  A hit

   216      /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-P6-13)

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/core_state.rs#L466-L513
   466  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-PERF-WALKMEMO)
   467  /// The slot count past which `take_walk_memo` hands back a FRESH table
   468  /// instead of a cleared one; see its note for how the value was chosen.
   469  pub const WALK_MEMO_KEEP: usize = 1 << 16;
   470  
   471  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean:386-388 Expr.allLevelParamsDefinedFast
   472  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/DeclCheck.lean:190-192 Expr.constsResolveFFast
   473  /// Lean twin: the `∅` that `proof/ConRon/Arena/CheckerBase.lean`'s
   474  /// `allLevelParamsDefined` and `constsResolveFFast` start their walk from —
   475  /// **the parked walk memo, moved out of the state and emptied** (task
   476  /// #97-PERF-WALKMEMO).  The slot is left holding `HashMap::new()` (which
   477  /// allocates nothing) for the length of the walk, and the entry puts the
   478  /// grown table back afterwards; either way the table this returns is empty,
   479  /// so the walk starts where the twin's does.
   480  ///
   481  /// **nanoda's guard** (`nanoda_lib/src/expr.rs`, `inst`): a table past
   482  /// `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` slots is dropped rather than kept, so that one huge walk
   483  /// does not leave a huge table behind for every later call.  `reset_map`'s
   484  /// `clear_fit` already decays such a table, one eighth of its high-water mark
   485  /// a call, so the guard only decides which of the two is cheaper for an
   486  /// outlier: re-growing from nothing, or `clear_fit`'s re-make at the decayed
   487  /// size.  The threshold, measured on `Init` (`--verified --jobs=1`, one
   488  /// `perf stat -e instructions:u` run each, all accepting 57 977):
   489  ///
   490  /// | `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` | instructions:u |
   491  /// |---|---:|
   492  /// | fresh `HashMap::new()` per call (before) | 211 976 016 505 |
   493  /// | 2^10 slots (nanoda's 1024) | 208 379 555 799 |
   494  /// | 2^12 | 206 572 063 910 |
   495  /// | 2^14 | 205 851 105 938 |
   496  /// | **2^16** | **205 785 515 243** |
   497  /// | no guard (2^60) | 205 783 023 575 |
   498  ///
   499  /// A guard low enough to trip on ordinary calls gives the saving back — at
   500  /// nanoda's 1024 more than half of it — because those calls re-grow by
   501  /// doubling, which is exactly the cost this table exists to avoid.  2^16 is
   502  /// the smallest power tried that costs nothing measurable on `Init` (2.5 M
   503  /// instructions over no guard), so it only ever fires on an outlier.
   504  pub fn take_walk_memo<K, V>(slot: &mut HashMap<K, V>) -> HashMap<K, V> {
   505      let m: HashMap<K, V> = core::mem::replace(slot, HashMap::new());
   506      if m.capacity() > WALK_MEMO_KEEP {
   507          HashMap::new()
   508      } else {
   509          let mut m2: HashMap<K, V> = m;
   510          reset_map(&mut m2);
   511          m2
   512      }
   513  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/hashmap2.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; a second `Std.HashMap` replacement, proved
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::HashMap2<K, V>` — proved in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean`
     4  //! (task #97-HM2; designed in task #97-P6-4b).  The same abstract object as
     5  //! `ron::hashmap`'s `HashMap` — a partial map from `K` to `V`, with
     6  //! `Hashable`/`Eq2`/`Dup` as its dictionaries and the same eleven operations
     7  //! — over an **open-addressed, epoch-stamped, flat slot vector** instead of
     8  //! the Aeneas tutorial's chained buckets.  `ron::hashmap` is untouched and
     9  //! keeps its proofs (`proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap.lean`); this module's are
    10  //! in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean` (task #97-HM2).
    11  //!
    12  //! **Why it exists.**  Task #97-P6-1 left `clear_slots + allocate_slots +
    13  //! move_elements*` at 21.8 % of `Init`, "all halving recursions over chained
    14  //! buckets".  Task #97-P6-4b counted what those recursions actually do on
    15  //! `Init`, and the counts name the representation rather than the code:
    16  //!
    17  //! | on `Init`, `ron::HashMap` | count |
    18  //! |---|---:|
    19  //! | `get` calls | 1 228 953 968 |
    20  //! | — resolved in 0 or 1 chain step | 98.8 % |
    21  //! | `insert` calls | 627 320 951 |
    22  //! | **`clear` calls** | **36 053 620** |
    23  //! | **— buckets walked by them** | **2 940 488 064** |
    24  //! | — entries those buckets held | 586 917 896 |
    25  //! | buckets pushed by `allocate_slots` | 948 184 512 |
    26  //! | entries moved by `move_elements*` | 349 323 629 |
    27  //!
    28  //! So the chains are *already* short — the table is a good hash table — and
    29  //! essentially all of the 21.8 % is the per-bucket cost of **emptying and
    30  //! re-growing** the slot vector: 2.94 G bucket writes to clear 0.59 G entries
    31  //! (five buckets walked per entry cleared; the average cleared table is 82
    32  //! buckets holding 16 entries) and 0.95 G `Vec::push`es to allocate them back.
    33  //! Nothing a better chain walk can do touches that.
    34  //!
    35  //! **The representation.**
    36  //!
    37  //! * `slots : Vec<Slot<K, V>>`, `Slot` = `Vacant | Live(u32, K, V)`.  No
    38  //!   `Box`, no chain, no allocation per entry — an entry *is* a slot.
    39  //! * A `Live` slot is **live only if its stamp is the table's `epoch`**;
    40  //!   a `Live` slot with a stale stamp is free space, indistinguishable from

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L326-L513

   331  /// con-leche: none — `FrontendClass` of a `CheckError` (see there).
   332  fn classify(e: &CheckError) -> FrontendClass {
   333      let m = con_ron::driver::message(e);
   334      match e {
   335          CheckError::NotImplemented(_) => FrontendClass::Declined(m),
   336          CheckError::Native(_) => FrontendClass::Declined(m),
   337          CheckError::Invalid(_) => FrontendClass::Invalid(m),
   338          CheckError::Internal(_) => FrontendClass::Internal(m),
   339      }
   340  }
   341  
   342  /// con-leche: none — a frontend failure's exit, one place: the decline, the
   343  /// reject and the internal error of the two frontend gates and of the
   344  /// preparation (con-leche writes the three arms out at each gate).
   345  fn frontend_exit(e: &CheckError, mode_tag: &str) -> u8 {
   346      match classify(e) {
   347          FrontendClass::Declined(what) => {
   348              eprintln!("con-ron: declined: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   349              2
   350          }
   351          FrontendClass::Invalid(what) => {
   352              eprintln!("con-ron: invalid: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   353              1
   354          }
   355          FrontendClass::Internal(msg) => {
   356              eprintln!("con-ron: {} ({})", msg, mode_tag);
   357              3
   358          }
   359      }
   360  }

   364  /// modules read from their `.olean` files along a search path.
   365  enum Input {
   366      Ndjson(String),
   367      Oleans(con_ron::olean_fs::OleanRequest),

   370  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:96-286 checkMainG
   371  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:86-94 readInputG
   372  /// The driver's front matter: the prelude, the streaming parse, the
   373  /// preparation, the pin walk, the receipts, then the fold and the verdict.
   374  /// It is the Lean twin's `runPipelineIO` with the heartbeat and the receipts
   375  /// around it (`Arena/Main.lean`), and `con-ron`'s `check_main` with the
   376  /// handles in place of the trees.
   377  fn check_main(a: &Args, input: &Input) -> u8 {
   378      let t0 = Instant::now();
   379      let mode_tag = if a.verified {
   380          "--verified"
   381      } else {
   382          "--trusted"
   383      };
   384      let mode = if a.verified {
   385          CheckMode::Verified
   386      } else {
   387          CheckMode::Trusted
   388      };
   389      // ONE store for the whole run: the prelude, the stream and the pins are
   390      // hash-consed together into its persistent tier (DESIGN.md §8.3).
   391      // ConRon.Capstone: `startState`
   392      let mut st = AState::empty();
   393      // THE PERSISTENT TIER a phase-B worker reads (DESIGN.md §8.3, task
   394      // #97-P6-6b).  The parse and phase A's setup own their own — the store
   395      // is owned (not frozen) outside a declaration bracket — so what they are
   396      // handed here is the EMPTY tier, and the single-lane computation is
   397      // unchanged.  Each phase-A bracket freezes the store and reads through
   398      // the tier it took out; phase B freezes the store's tier into a
   399      // `PersTier` and hands `&` it to every worker; `check_decls_driver` is
   400      // where that happens.
   401      // ConRon.Capstone: `emptyTier`
   402      let pers: &PersTier = &PersTier::empty();
   403      // THE RESERVED-NAME PINS, interned once into that persistent tier before
   404      // anything else touches it (task #97-P6-4a, `arena::pins`): the scratch
   405      // tier is closed here, so every pinned handle is persistent and survives
   406      // every `drop_scratch` of the run.  Until this has run, every `pin_*`
   407      // read raises `Internal` rather than answering — which is what makes the
   408      // initialisation-order hazard task #97c named impossible rather than
   409      // unlikely.
   410      // ConRon.Capstone: h1
   411      match con_ron_core::arena::pins::intern_reserved_pins(pers, &mut st) {
   412          Ok(()) => (),
   413          Err(e) => {
   414              eprintln!(
   415                  "con-ron: the reserved-name pins do not intern ({}) ({})",
   416                  con_ron::driver::message(&e),
   417                  mode_tag
   418              );
   419              return 3;
   420          }
   421      }
   422      // THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE, parsed into that store before anything else.
   423      // ConRon.Capstone: h2
   424      let prelude_ix = match prelude::builtin_prelude_e(pers, &mut st) {
   425          Ok(p) => p,
   426          Err((e, line)) => {
   427              let what = match classify(&e) {
   428                  FrontendClass::Internal(m) => format!("does not parse (line {}: {})", line, m),
   429                  FrontendClass::Declined(w) => format!("is unsupported ({})", w),
   430                  FrontendClass::Invalid(w) => format!("contradicts itself ({})", w),
   431              };
   432              eprintln!(
   433                  "con-ron: the built-in prelude {}; regenerate it with \
   434                   `lake exe natop-pins-export` ({})",
   435                  what, mode_tag
   436              );
   437              return 3;
   438          }
   439      };
   440      // Streaming frontend: the file is read 4 MiB at a time and each buffer is
   441      // parsed and dropped, so neither a wholesale text buffer nor a scratch
   442      // file exists.  What comes out is the FILE's records as HANDLES into the
   443      // store above.  No model is ever read from the input: every inductive
   444      // block — mutual and nested included — installs through the kernel's
   445      // uniform installer, unconditionally (task #105).
   446      // ConRon.Capstone: hreads, h3 (`parse_source` over the file's handle)
   447      // The `.olean` path ends in the same records (task #142); no capstone
   448      // premise is about it yet (OVERVIEW.md).
   449      let read: std::io::Result<Result<ParseResultD, (CheckError, u64)>> = match input {
   450          Input::Ndjson(file) => match driver::parse_export_stream_d(pers, &mut st, file, export_c::CHUNK_SIZE) {
   451              Err(e) => {
   452                  eprintln!("con-ron: {}: {}", con_ron::render::display_path(file), e);
   453                  return 3;
   454              }
   455              Ok((r, _)) => Ok(r),
   456          },
   457          Input::Oleans(req) => Ok(con_ron::olean_fs::read_request(pers, &mut st, req)),
   458      };
   459      let label: String = match input {
   460          Input::Ndjson(file) => con_ron::render::display_path(file),
   461          Input::Oleans(req) => req.label(pers, &st),
   462      };
   463      let parsed: ParseResultD = match read {
   464          Err(_) => return 3,
   465          Ok(Err((e, line))) => match classify(&e) {
   466              FrontendClass::Declined(what) => {
   467                  eprintln!("con-ron: declined: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   468                  return 2;
   469              }
   470              // A stream whose inductive block contradicts its own declarations
   471              // in a REDUNDANT field is rejected at the parse.
   472              FrontendClass::Invalid(what) => {
   473                  eprintln!("con-ron: invalid: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   474                  return 1;
   475              }
   476              FrontendClass::Internal(msg) => {
   477                  eprintln!("con-ron: {}:{}: {}", label, line, msg);
   478                  return 3;
   479              }
   480          },
   481          Ok(Ok(r)) => r,
   482      };
   483      let file_records = parsed.decls.len();
   484      // From here on the store is the checker's state: the memo tables and the
   485      // per-declaration caches join it (`AState`), and every handle the parse
   486      // produced indexes into it.
   487      // **PREPARE** (`frontend::prepare`): what the fold runs over is
   488      // `prepare_prelude` of the file's records — the prelude's declarations
   489      // first (the stream's own copies where it has them, the rest synthesised),
   490      // then the stream's, with every pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
   491      // ground hoisted ahead of it.  It takes the whole state since task
   492      // #97-P4d: step 2 is the real ground hoist, which interns.
   493      // ConRon.Capstone: h4
   494      let prepared = match prepare::prepare_d(pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed.decls) {
   495          Ok(p) => p,
   496          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   497      };
   498      // the ground hoist's receipt
   499      if !prepared.hoisted.is_empty() {
   500          let names: Vec<String> = prepared
   501              .hoisted
   502              .iter()
   503              .map(|n| driver::name_of(pers, &st.store, n))
   504              .collect();
   505          eprintln!(
   506              "con-ron: {} declarations hoisted ahead of the pinned Nat operations \
   507               they ground: {}",
   508              prepared.hoisted.len(),
   509              names.join(", ")
   510          );
   511      }
   512      // ConRon.Capstone: hpins (`decode_embedded`; `--pins`/`--no-pins` are
   513      // outside the theorems)

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/pins.rs#L1-L60
     1  //! `arena::pins` — the reserved names, interned ONCE (task #97-P6-4a).
     2  //!
     3  //! con-leche compares its reserved names — `natName`, `natZeroName`,
     4  //! `natSuccName`, the sixteen `Nat`-operation names, the `Bool` trio, the
     5  //! `String`/`List`/`Char` family, the standard and the trusted axiom names —
     6  //! as `Name` VALUES, which Lean builds once per nullary `def` and caches.
     7  //! The arena compares them as HANDLES, so `arena::core::pin` turned each one
     8  //! into `intern_name` of a freshly built `Name`: a `code_points` allocation
     9  //! and an `Arc<NameNode>` per path segment, then one cons-table probe per
    10  //! segment, every time.  Task #97-P6-1's counter measured what that costs on
    11  //! `Init`: **140 083 646 `NStore::intern` calls, of which 88 854 033 are
    12  //! probes of a `str` node built purely to be compared and dropped** — tens of
    13  //! millions of rebuilds of about forty constants, in `natLitSupported`'s
    14  //! three probes per literal, in `natOpNames`, in `strLitToConstructor`.
    15  //!
    16  //! This module is DESIGN.md's answer, flagged at task #97c ("the `Pins`
    17  //! record that is NOT here") and deferred there for want of a number: one
    18  //! record, filled once at the driver by `intern_reserved_pins`, and every
    19  //! `pin` of a constant name becomes a field read.
    20  //!
    21  //! **Not `arena::checker`'s `intern_all_pins`.**  That one walks the `--pins`
    22  //! RECEIPT file (the trusted pin list) into the persistent tier; this one
    23  //! interns the checker's own reserved constants.  The two run at the same
    24  //! point of the pipeline and mean different things, which is why they have
    25  //! different names.
    26  //!
    27  //! ## The table is a `Vec`, and that is what kills task #97c's hazard
    28  //!
    29  //! Task #97c declined the record because of an initialisation-order hazard:
    30  //! "a pin read before it is filled compares against the zero word and
    31  //! silently says *not `Nat`*".  A record of handle FIELDS has that hazard,
    32  //! because every 32-bit word is a syntactically valid handle.  A `Vec<NIdx>`
    33  //! does not: before `intern_reserved_pins` runs the table is EMPTY, so `pin_at`
    34  //! takes its bounds branch and raises `CheckError::Internal` — a loud stop,
    35  //! never a quiet wrong answer.  The cost is one `len` compare per read,
    36  //! against an interning walk it replaces.
    37  //!
    38  //! ## What is pinned
    39  //!
    40  //! The fifty-one names below and `basis_names::reserved_basis_names()`'s
    41  //! sixteen, plus the three interned values every `pin` site around them
    42  //! needs: the empty universe-argument list, the level `0` and the expression
    43  //! `Sort 1` (`arena::core`'s `empty_levels`, `zero_level` and `sort_one`,
    44  //! which now read this record instead of interning).
    45  //!
    46  //! All of them go into the PERSISTENT tier, because `intern_reserved_pins` runs
    47  //! before the parse, while the scratch tier is closed.  That matters twice:
    48  //! a pinned handle must survive every `drop_scratch` (it is read across all
    49  //! of them), and task #97-P6-1's `pers_find_maybe` rests on "a persistent
    50  //! node's children are persistent", which the bottom-up intern of a closed
    51  //! scratch tier gives for free.
    52  //!
    53  //! **Denotation unchanged.**  A pin is `intern_name` of the same `Name`, so
    54  //! the handle this record holds is the handle `pin` computed before —
    55  //! `denoteN` is injective and `intern` is idempotent, so pre-interning a name
    56  //! the export also carries hands the export's parse the very same handle.
    57  //! What changes is only WHEN the intern happens, and how many times.
    58  //!
    59  //! Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:118-135 AState` (DESIGN.md §8.6's
    60  //! twin ledger, task #97-P6-4a) — `AState` gains a `pins : Pins` field and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/frontend/prepare.rs#L1-L50
     1  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/Prepare.lean` — **what happens between the
     2  //! file and the fold** (task #97 P4e part 1).
     3  //!
     4  //! `prepare_prelude` is total — no record of the stream is dropped, rewritten
     5  //! or retagged — and it does two things:
     6  //!
     7  //! 1. **the prelude's declarations first**, the stream's OWN copy of each
     8  //!    where the stream has one and a synthesised one only where it has none,
     9  //!    so a stream that declares the toolchain's `Bool` is checked on its own
    10  //!    `Bool` record;
    11  //! 2. **the ground hoist**: a pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
    12  //!    structural ground is moved ahead of it when the stream declares it
    13  //!    later.
    14  //!
    15  //! Moving a record earlier can only reject, never accept, which is why the
    16  //! spec con-leche proves is as simple as it is:
    17  //!
    18  //! ```text
    19  //! ∃ extra, (∀ d ∈ extra, d ∈ prelude) ∧
    20  //!   (preparePrelude ds).toList.Perm (ds.toList ++ extra)
    21  //! ```
    22  //!
    23  //! **Step 2 is `frontend::nat_op_ground`'s**, a module of its own exactly as
    24  //! con-leche's is (task #97-P4d; task #97-P4e part 1 shipped an identity
    25  //! placeholder here, because the pass needs the kernel's
    26  //! `natOpNames`/`natDivModNames`, which arrived with the pins).  It is why
    27  //! `prepare_d` takes the whole `AState` where everything else in this module
    28  //! needs only the store.
    29  //!
    30  //! **Where the store comes from.**  Only `prelude_key`, whose `.anonymous`
    31  //! fall-through has to be INTERNED, and the two functions that call it;
    32  //! [`pick_idx`] and [`declares`] are pure, exactly as con-leche's are, because
    33  //! `env::i_declaration_names` is.
    34  //! Nothing in this module reads or writes a term.
    35  //!
    36  //! **The deviation of the port into the verified core** (task #84), kept
    37  //! verbatim from `con_ron_core::frontend::prepare`: con-leche's `pick` ERASES
    38  //! the picked record from the array (`Array.eraseIdxIfInBounds`) and `frontOf`
    39  //! moves it to the front.  The Aeneas subset has no operation that takes an
    40  //! element out of a `Vec` — no `remove`, no `pop`, no `into_iter` — so the
    41  //! port splits the two halves that con-leche fuses: [`pick_idx`] is the cited
    42  //! `ds.findIdx (declares n)` with the erasure recorded in a `picked` mask
    43  //! instead of performed, [`front_of`] runs that over the prelude, and
    44  //! [`prepared_stream`] materialises the whole prepared list in ONE pass.  The
    45  //! list that comes out is the same list; the cost is one record copy per
    46  //! record, where the copied fields are handles and `Vec` spines and not terms.
    47  //! con-leche's `pickSpec`/`frontSpec` are not ported (they are `cons`-list
    48  //! specifications with no caller on the run path); `pick_spec` lives in this
    49  //! module's tests, where it still checks `pick_idx` against the specification
    50  //! on every `cargo test`.

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L961-L1002
   961  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:170-178 foldChunks
   962  /// **The file handle as the parse's `ChunkSource`**: each `next_chunk` is one
   963  /// `read_up_to` of `chunk` bytes, strictly forward, handed over whole; the
   964  /// first empty read is the end of the input.  A failed read ends the input
   965  /// the same way and is KEPT here, and `parse_export_handle_d` reports it in
   966  /// place of whatever the parse of the truncated input said — so a read error
   967  /// is exit 3, never a verdict, as before the loop moved.
   968  pub struct HandleSource<'a, R: Read> {
   969      /// The open reader.
   970      pub h: &'a mut R,
   971      /// The buffer size, `export_c::CHUNK_SIZE` in the binary.
   972      pub chunk: usize,
   973      /// The nonempty buffers handed out so far, for the heartbeat.
   974      pub chunks: u64,
   975      /// The first read failure, if any.
   976      pub err: Option<std::io::Error>,
   977  }
   978  
   979  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:170-178 foldChunks
   980  impl<'a, R: Read> ChunkSource for HandleSource<'a, R> {
   981      /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:170-178 foldChunks
   982      /// One read of up to `chunk` bytes; empty at the end or on a failure.
   983      fn next_chunk(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
   984          if self.err.is_some() {
   985              return Vec::new();
   986          }
   987          let mut buf: Vec<u8> = vec![0u8; self.chunk];
   988          match read_up_to(self.h, &mut buf) {
   989              Ok(n) => {
   990                  buf.truncate(n);
   991                  if n > 0 {
   992                      self.chunks += 1;
   993                  }
   994                  buf
   995              }
   996              Err(e) => {
   997                  self.err = Some(e);
   998                  Vec::new()
   999              }
  1000          }
  1001      }
  1002  }

     1  //! `arena::checker` — the declaration fold, over handles.
     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean`, which is con-leche's
     4  //! `Kernel/Checker.lean`'s `checkDecl`/`checkDeclsPure` and
     5  //! `Cached/Installed.lean`'s two-phase `checkDecls`.
     6  //!
     7  //! ## Two folds, and which is which
     8  //!
     9  //! * **`check_decls_pure`** is the THEOREM's shape —
    10  //!   `ConLeche/Model/Fold.lean`'s `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` consumes it, and
    11  //!   DESIGN.md §8.2's Theorem 1 folds `checkDecl` over the stream.  One step
    12  //!   per record, install and check together.
    13  //! * **`install_then_check`** is what the BINARY runs: phase A installs every
    14  //!   record, guarding its header and its value but not inferring, and pushes an
    15  //!   inductive block as stored (`inductives::stored_install`); phase B runs the
    16  //!   jobs, in fold order: each recorded declaration's check against the PREFIX
    17  //!   VIEW it was installed at, and each block's checked install, compared with
    18  //!   its stored pushes (`block_check`).  con-leche proves the two are the same
    19  //!   accept (`fullyChecked_checkDecls`); the arena's two call the same
    20  //!   `checkDecl` pieces, which is what keeps them the same computation.
    21  //!
    22  //! ## Every step is bracketed
    23  //!
    24  //! DESIGN.md §8.3: "Persistent = parse + installed environment; scratch = one
    25  //! declaration's check."  Both phases and both folds run each record inside
    26  //! `enter_scratch` … `drop_scratch`.  Phase B's `check_pending` brackets
    27  //! `check_value_group`, and every node it appends goes with the tier.  Phase
    28  //! A's `install_step` brackets the install too (the fallback
    29  //! `install_step_other` included), because the ordinary step's installers
    30  //! infer and inference interns: `promote` copies exactly what leaves the step
    31  //! — the installed constants and the pending record — to the persistent tier
    32  //! before the drop (see `install_step`).
    33  //! `check_decls_pure`'s step, `check_decl_step`, is bracketed the same way.  An
    34  //! inductive block's stored install has brackets of its own
    35  //! (`inductives::stored_install`'s note).
    36  //!
    37  //! ## The pins are interned at startup
    38  //!
    39  //! `intern_all_pins` is DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d's one-time tree walk, and it is what
    40  //! makes every later `pin`/`intern_ci` of the same datum return the PERSISTENT
    41  //! handle whatever tier is live (§8.3: `intern` probes the persistent table

   218  /// ```
   219  ///
   220  /// `promote` (`arena::promote`) is the memoised structural copy scratch →
   221  /// persistent, run on **exactly what leaves the step**: the `k` constants and
   222  /// the `kt` projection tables the step installed (`promote_new`) and the
   223  /// pending record (`promote_vg`, at the

   227  /// (`installGuardsC` and the `.thmDecl` arm's own `flushC`, and

   229  pub fn install_step(
   230      _pers: &PersTier,
   231      st: &mut AState,
   232      mode: &CheckMode,
   233      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   234      i: u64,

   244      match install_step_go(&tier, st, mode, pins, fe, pd) {

   247              Err(e)

   250              scratch_restore(st, saved);

   259                      Ok((_, fe3)) => {
   260                          drop_scratch(st, tier);
   261                          Ok((fe3, pend))
   262                      }
   263                  },
   264                  Some(vg) => install_step_promote(tier, st, i, vis, k, kt, fe2, pend, vg),

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/inductives/stored_install.rs#L1-L50
     1  //! `arena::inductives::stored_install` — the stored install of an inductive
     2  //! block, and the comparison of what an install pushes.
     3  //!
     4  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Inductives/StoredInstall.lean`, which
     5  //! is `ConLeche/Cached/StoredInstall.lean` over handles.  Phase A pushes an
     6  //! inductive block **as the input stores it**: every constant and table is read
     7  //! off the block's records, and nothing is generated.  The block's checked
     8  //! install runs later, as a job of the check phase (`checker::block_check`),
     9  //! and compares what it pushes with what this install pushed; a difference is
    10  //! an internal error (this reading is wrong, the stream is not).
    11  //!
    12  //! What is read, and from where (the checked install's own functions on the
    13  //! same inputs wherever one exists):
    14  //!
    15  //! * the formers: each at its telescope, with `block_caps_at` at official's
    16  //!   `is_rec` and member 0's result sort.  The telescope is the stored type
    17  //!   where that is a syntactic telescope ending in a sort, else the reduced
    18  //!   telescope official's `whnf` loop reads;
    19  //! * the constructors as declared;
    20  //! * the recursors: each at its stored type, its stored right-hand sides, its
    21  //!   rules' metadata by `tgt_stored_rules` at the record's major;
    22  //! * the projection tables: the bodies by substitution, the guards (the
    23  //!   fields' sorts) inferred here by the constructor stage's own walk.
    24  //!
    25  //! Where a part cannot be read it is pushed at its record as declared (a
    26  //! former, a recursor's rules) or left out (a table): the block is one the
    27  //! checked install rejects, and its job reports it.
    28  //!
    29  //! ## The twin's deviations
    30  //!
    31  //! * **The reading's two inferences each have a scratch bracket of their own**
    32  //!   (`stored_tele_slow`, `stored_guards`): a failed inference is a VALUE here,
    33  //!   `None` or no guards, and the run goes on, so the state after one must be
    34  //!   the state it started from.  The bracket gives exactly that: nothing writes
    35  //!   the persistent tier inside it, its `Err` arm (`stored_abandon`) writes the state
    36  //!   from the tier and the saved pins, with empty memos, caches and scratch, and what an
    37  //!   accepted inference leaves is promoted before the drop.  Everything else of
    38  //!   the reading runs in one bracket at its end (`stored_tail`), which promotes
    39  //!   the block's new constants and tables as `install_step`'s does.
    40  //! * **A term comparison is handle equality**, since a term is hash-consed
    41  //!   across the tiers: con-leche's pointer-first `Expr` equality with no
    42  //!   fallback.  The comparisons are one function per type: there are no
    43  //!   closures, so `listBeqBy` is a walk per list.
    44  //! * **The store's own failures stay failures** (a full handle space, a
    45  //!   dangling handle): they are what `Native`/`Internal` are for, a stop of
    46  //!   phase A at this record (`checker::phase_a_failure`).
    47  //! * **A name already taken stops phase A here** (`M_SLOT_TAKEN`), before
    48  //!   anything is pushed, and the block's job is run for the verdict:
    49  //!   `ParInstall.lean`'s `commitLoop`, at the slot that does not match.
    50

   755                  Ok(())
   756              } else {
   757                  fail(CheckError::Internal(code_points(&M_PUSHES_DIFFER)))

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L548-L648
   548  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:317-334 checkDecls
   549  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/Run.lean:50-210 checkDeclsIO
   550  /// **The driver**: the two-phase fold with the boundary visible — a straight
   551  /// line of calls, with the observer's lines between them and the pool for
   552  /// phase B, at every job count.  Each step is one premise of the capstone:
   553  ///
   554  /// | step | here | the capstone's premise |
   555  /// |---|---|---|
   556  /// | phase A | `checker::install_fold_hooked(…, fold_start(), ds, 0, obs)` | the same call accepts |
   557  /// | boundary | `checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store, fe)` | the same call's value |
   558  /// | phase B | `pool::parallel_all(m, workers, ‖ worker_state(pins), ‖w, k‖ run_job(&tier, w, mode, &layer, &pend, &blocks, &order[k]), …)` | `h8`: index lists `ws` covering `0..order.len`, each `w` a `foldlM` of `run_job` over `k ∈ w` from `worker_state pins`, accepting (internally `ParallelAll`) |
   559  /// | after | `checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier)` | restores the store and hands `fe` back (`freeze_tier_ok`) |
   560  ///
   561  /// `init` and `step` are calls into the verified crate; `parallel_all` is the
   562  /// one trusted piece, and its contract (`pool.rs`'s note) is exactly
   563  /// `ParallelAll`: on `Ok`, every job was run by some worker, each worker folding
   564  /// `run_job` over the jobs it claimed on ONE `worker_state`.  Everything else
   565  /// here is the observer, which only ever holds `&` the state (the hook of phase
   566  /// A by the trait's own signature, the other lines through `&st.store` and the
   567  /// worker's `&AState`), so it cannot change an outcome.
   568  ///
   569  /// **Phase A failing** runs the block jobs before it (`checker::phase_a_failure`):
   570  /// a stored block is checked only by its job, and a failure past it may be that
   571  /// block's doing, so the verdict is the first failing job's.  **Phase B** merges
   572  /// the value checks and the block jobs in fold order (`checker::job_order`), and
   573  /// the pool reports the least failing index, so the first failure in fold order
   574  /// is the verdict at every job count.
   575  ///
   576  /// **The boundary is where the tier is FROZEN.**  Phase A owns its persistent
   577  /// tier and its index and appends to them; at the boundary `checker::freeze_tier`
   578  /// moves the four stores' persistent tables and the index into one `PersTier`,
   579  /// handed back `frozen`: every read through it goes to those tables, and a
   580  /// worker's own store is frozen (`checker::worker_state`), so every append there
   581  /// is a scratch append.  So `n` workers share one environment and one term DAG and
   582  /// own nothing but a scratch tier, their caches and a copy of the pin handles.
   583  pub fn check_decls_driver<O: PhaseObserver + InstallHook + Send>(
   584      pers: &PersTier,
   585      st: &mut AState,
   586      mode: &CheckMode,
   587      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   588      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   589      jobs: u64,
   590      obs: &mut O,
   591  ) -> Result<IFEnv, (CheckError, u64)> {
   592      let total = ds.len();
   593      // PHASE A (ConRon.Capstone: h6): the verified fold, the heartbeat as hook.
   594      let p = match checker::install_fold_hooked(pers, st, mode, pins, checker::fold_start(), ds, 0, &*obs) {
   595          Err((e, i)) => {
   596              let f = checker::phase_a_failure(pers, st, mode, pins, ds, e, i);
   597              obs.install_failed(f.1, total);
   598              return Err(f);
   599          }
   600          Ok(p) => p,
   601      };
   602      let (_n_installed, fe, pend, blocks): (u64, IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>, Vec<BlockCheck>) = p;
   603      let order: Vec<(bool, u64)> = checker::job_order(&pend, &blocks);  // ConRon.Capstone: hord
   604      let m = order.len();
   605      obs.install_done(pers, &st.store, total, m, blocks.len());
   606      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   607      obs.phase_b_workers(workers);
   608      // THE PHASE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier and the index leave the state and
   609      // become a value every worker reads (the doc comment above).  `st` keeps its
   610      // (empty) store, its tables moved out, so the observer can still read a
   611      // label back through the tier.  (ConRon.Capstone: h7)
   612      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store, fe);
   613      let layer: IFEnv = checker::check_layer();  // ConRon.Capstone: hlayer
   614      // PHASE B: `run_job` at every job, on `workers` threads, each folding it over
   615      // the jobs it claims on ONE `worker_state` — the verdict and the record a
   616      // rejection names are the one-worker walk's at every `--jobs` (the least
   617      // failing index).  (ConRon.Capstone: h8)
   618      let heartbeat = obs.wants_check_lines();
   619      let lock: Mutex<(usize, &mut O)> = Mutex::new((0, obs));
   620      let r = parallel_all(
   621          m,
   622          workers,
   623          || checker::worker_state(&st.pins),
   624          |w: &mut AState, k| checker::run_job(&tier, w, mode, &layer, &pend, &blocks, &order[k]),
   625          |w: &AState, k| check_line(heartbeat, &lock, &tier, w, m, &job_at(&order, &pend, &blocks, k)),
   626      );
   627      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   628          Ok((_, o)) => o,
   629          Err(e) => e.into_inner().1,
   630      };
   631      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the fold — the verdict line's
   632      // declaration label, the failing record's name, the receipts — reads a
   633      // handle back out of `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has
   634      // gone out of scope answers `None` to every one of them (the first
   635      // version of this printed `at theorem ?` where the tip printed `at
   636      // theorem addOk`).  `thaw_tier` is `freeze_tier` inverted.
   637      let fe: IFEnv = checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   638      match phase_b_verdict(&order, &pend, &blocks, r) {
   639          Err((e, pos)) => {
   640              obs.check_failed(pos);
   641              Err((e, pos))
   642          }
   643          Ok(()) => {
   644              obs.check_done(m);
   645              Ok(fe)
   646          }
   647      }
   648  }

    30  //! ## What a worker is, in phase B
    31  //!
    32  //! §8.3 has said since P1 what phase B is: "the persistent tier is immutable
    33  //! in phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — **no atomics anywhere**",
    34  //! and task #97-P6-6 verified it in the code (`check_pending` is the bracket;
    35  //! the persistent interns' only caller is phase A's `arena::promote`, which
    36  //! writes a `&mut PersTier` a worker never holds).  So the driver's `init`
    37  //! builds `checker::worker_state(pins)` — an EMPTY store, FROZEN

    39  //! and `Caches`, and a COPY of
    40  //! the driver's `Pins` — and its `step` borrows the frozen `&PersTier`, which
    41  //! holds the installed index.  A value check reads it at its prefix bound, a
    42  //! scalar (`pc.vis`), through one shared empty layer; a block job pushes into a
    43  //! layer of its own over it.  So a worker costs no environment copy at all.

   227  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:236-269 checkPool
   228  /// **`step` at every index of `0..n`, on a pool of `workers` threads** — the
   229  /// module note's trusted claim is this function's contract:
   230  ///
   231  /// > If it returns `Ok(())`, every index in `0..n` was claimed by exactly one
   232  /// > worker, each worker built its state with `init()` once and folded `step`
   233  /// > over its claimed indices in claim order (increasing), and every step
   234  /// > returned `Ok(())`.
   235  ///
   236  /// On a failure it returns the LEAST failing index with its error
   237  /// (`ParallelError::Step`), whatever the timing.  `after(&st, k)` runs on the
   238  /// worker's thread after each step it made, with the worker's state by `&`
   239  /// (the driver's heartbeat); it cannot change an outcome.
   240  ///
   241  /// The workers are `std::thread::scope`d, with `STACK_BYTES` of stack each.
   242  /// `workers` is the count the caller has already clamped
   243  /// (`driver::workers_for`: `max(1, min(jobs, n))`); if the OS refuses to
   244  /// spawn one, the pool runs on those it has, and on the calling thread if it
   245  /// has none — the contract holds at every worker count, so the answer does
   246  /// not depend on it.
   247  pub fn parallel_all<S, E: Send>(
   248      n: usize,
   249      workers: usize,
   250      init: impl Fn() -> S + Sync,
   251      step: impl Fn(&mut S, usize) -> Result<(), E> + Sync,
   252      after: impl Fn(&S, usize) + Sync,
   253  ) -> Result<(), ParallelError<E>> {
