   185  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:256-375 Expr — the fuel-indexed
   186  readback of an expression handle. -/
   187  def denoteEAux (st : EStore) : Nat → EIdx → Option Expr
   188    | 0, _ => none
   189    | f + 1, i =>
   190      (st.view i).bind fun v =>
   191        match v with
   192        | .bvar k => some (.bvar k)
   193        | .fvar k ty => (denoteEAux st f ty).map (Expr.fvar k)
   194        | .sort u => (denoteL st.ls u).map Expr.sort
   195        | .const n us => opt2 Expr.const (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteLs st.lss us)
   196        | .app g a => opt2 Expr.app (denoteEAux st f g) (denoteEAux st f a)
   197        | .lam ty b => opt2 Expr.lam (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   198        | .forallE ty b => opt2 Expr.forallE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   199        | .letE ty w b =>
   200          opt3 Expr.letE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f w) (denoteEAux st f b)
   201        | .lit l => some (.lit l)
   202        | .proj n k e =>
   203          opt2 (fun nm x => Expr.proj nm k x) (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteEAux st f e)
   204  
   205  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:256-375 Expr — the readback of an
   206  expression handle, at the store's own node count as fuel. -/
   207  def denoteE (st : EStore) (i : EIdx) : Option Expr :=
   208    denoteEAux st (st.nodeCount + 1) i

== proof/ConRon/Arena/WF.lean#L1-L39
     1  /-
     2  # Store well-formedness and the store layer's theorems (DESIGN.md §8.3, P2a)
     3  
     4  `StoreWF` is the arena's own invariant — con-leche's `TWF`
     5  (`Setlec/Kernel/ArenaWF.lean:900`, 28 clauses) redrawn for the
     6  per-constructor, high-tag representation.  It lives here, beside the
     7  implementation, importing nothing from `ConRon.Refine`: con-leche's lesson 27,
     8  "implementation may import a *self-contained* data-structure verification".
     9  
    10  Each store's invariant is `∃ rank, …WFAt st rank`.  The rank is existential
    11  because nothing at runtime stores it (DESIGN §8.3: "zero runtime cost, and no
    12  global array order is needed with per-constructor arrays"); what it buys is
    13  
    14  * **acyclicity**, hence a terminating `denote`;
    15  * **a fuel bound**: a persistent node's rank is below the persistent node
    16    count and a scratch node's below the total, so `nodeCount + 1` — the fuel
    17    `denoteE` uses — is always enough, and `dropScratch` shrinks both sides of
    18    the persistent clause together.
    19  
    20  The clauses, in the order a reader meets them:
    21  
    22  | clause | what it says |
    23  |---|---|
    24  | `childOK` | every child is in range, ranked below its parent, and persistent if the parent is |
    25  | `rankP` / `rankS` | ranks are below the tier's node count (the fuel bound) |
    26  | `consP` / `consS` | each tier's cons table is exactly the inverse of that tier's `get` |
    27  | `fresh` | a scratch cons entry never duplicates a persistent one (DESIGN §8.3's cross-tier canonicity; con-leche's `t_cons_fresh`) |
    28  | `derExact` | the derived column is `derOfView` of the node — *locally*; the global `derived st i = e.data` is a theorem (`derived_exact`) |
    29  | `sized` | the derived array is as long as the node array |
    30  | `cap` | no constructor array exceeds its handle shape's index range (2^30 for `app`, 2^26 for the rest), so the index is injective on it |
    31  | `scrOff` | the scratch tier is empty while the scratch flag is off |
    32  | `sync` | the nesting's scratch flags move together (task #97a) |
    33  
    34  `childOK`'s third conjunct — *persistent parents have persistent children* —
    35  is what makes `dropScratch` sound: without it a persistent node could point
    36  into a tier that is about to vanish.  It needs no hypothesis at `intern`,
    37  because `scrOff` makes a scratch handle undecodable while the flag is off, so
    38  a valid child of a node appended to the persistent tier is persistent already.
    39  -/

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Specs.lean#L1-L31
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Bridge.Specs` — one `@[spec]` theorem per `Monad.lean` primitive
     3  
     4  **One spec theorem per (B) primitive, in one shape**, so that the
     5  verification-condition generator (`vcgen`, on native `Std.WP` triples) can
     6  walk a twin's body without any store reasoning appearing in the proof text.
     7  The shape is the seven-rule template (DESIGN §8.6, `P2s SPIKE`, and task
     8  #97s's section):
     9  
    10  ```lean
    11  @[spec] theorem f_spec (s₀ : AState) (args…) (pre…) :
    12      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ f args ⦃fun r s' => Post s₀ r s'; ⊤⦄
    13  ```
    14  
    15  1. **the precondition is `s = s₀` and nothing else** — every real
    16     precondition is an ordinary hypothesis of the theorem, so `vcgen` turns it
    17     into a side goal instead of an entailment to discharge in the logic;
    18  2. **exception postcondition `⊤` (partial correctness), never the default
    19     `⊥`** (`⦃P⦄ x ⦃Q⦄` is TOTAL correctness in `Std.WP`) — a (B) function may
    20     fail and Theorem 1 claims nothing then (con-leche's `SimAt`,
    21     `Verify/SimI.lean:244`);
    22  3. **the postcondition names `s₀`**, the only way to state
    23     `Ext s₀.store s'.store` in a triple;
    24  4. **"the subject denotes" is an `isSome`, never a named `Expr`**;
    25  5. **the answer is a named relation or predicate** (`Rel.lean`'s `RelE`
    26     family, `Grind.lean`'s `Ans`/`MapRel`), never a bare `∀ e, … → …`;
    27  6. **a memo insert's spec states that the INVARIANT is preserved**, not that
    28     the table grew — the rule that matters most;
    29  7. **one named failure primitive** (`fail`): every failure site goes
    30     through it, so one spec covers them all and the Rust has one function to
    31     match.

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Run.lean#L60-L76
    60  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/SimI.lean:244 SimAt — **the PURE grade's
    61  statement**: from a well-formed store, an ACCEPTING run of the twin returns an
    62  answer related to the pure side's by `R`, having only grown the arena.
    63  
    64  Partial correctness, as everywhere in this library: a (B) function may fail
    65  and Theorem 1 claims nothing then — which is why the hypothesis is
    66  `c s0 = .ok (r, s')` and not an unconditional equation.
    67  
    68  **RUN form rather than a Hoare triple** (DESIGN `### Task #97-P3-Checker`
    69  §1): this tier's work is composition, inversion and list induction rather
    70  than verification conditions, and the checker tier that consumes `IndSpec`
    71  (`Bridge/Checker/Arms.lean`) is written in run form too (`AM.bind_ok` is its
    72  inversion). -/

    74      Prop :=
    75    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), StateOK s₀ → P s₀.store → c s₀ = .ok (r, s') →
    76      PStep s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/StructParts.lean#L125-L171
   125  /-! ## The spines -/
   126  
   127  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/StructParts.lean:52-53 structPsAt
   128  The parameter variables as seen from under `o` extra binders.
   129  
   130  **Proof:** a `Nat` recursion over
   131  `internBVarE_run` with the cursor `k` generalised.  The pure side is a
   132  `List.range` map, so the step is `List.range_succ_eq_map` and one `omega` on
   133  the index arithmetic (`k + (j + 1) = k + 1 + j`). -/
   134  theorem structPsAt_go_run (o nP : Nat) : ∀ (n k : Nat) {s s' : AState}
   135      {r : List EIdx}, StateOK s → Arena.structPsAt.go o nP n k s = .ok (r, s') →
   136      PStep s s' ∧ Frontend.denoteEList s'.store r
   137        = some ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j))) := by
   138    intro n
   139    induction n with
   140    | zero =>
   141      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   142      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   143      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok hrun
   144      exact ⟨PStep.refl hok, rfl⟩
   145    | succ n ih =>
   146      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   147      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   148      obtain ⟨b, s₁, h1, h2⟩ := AM.bind_ok hrun
   149      obtain ⟨rest, s₂, h3, h4⟩ := AM.bind_ok h2
   150      obtain ⟨hstep1, hb⟩ := internBVarE_run hok h1
   151      obtain ⟨hstep2, hrest⟩ := ih (k + 1) hstep1.ok h3
   152      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok h4
   153      refine ⟨hstep1.trans hstep2, ?_⟩
   154      have hkey : ((List.range (n + 1)).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j)))
   155          = Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - k) ::
   156            ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + 1 + j))) := by
   157        rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.map_cons, List.map_map]
   158        congr 1
   159        refine List.map_congr_left (fun j _ => ?_)
   160        simp only [Function.comp_apply]
   161        congr 1
   162        omega
   163      rw [hkey]
   164      simp only [Frontend.denoteEList, denote_ext hb hstep2.ext, hrest]
   165  
   166  theorem structPsAt_spec (o nP : Nat) :
   167      PSpec PT (Arena.structPsAt o nP) (REL (ConLeche.structPsAt o nP)) := by
   168    intro s₀ s' r hok _ hrun
   169    obtain ⟨hstep, hd⟩ := structPsAt_go_run o nP nP 0 hok hrun
   170    refine ⟨hstep, ?_⟩
   171    simpa only [ConLeche.structPsAt, Nat.zero_add] using hd

   112  structure KnotSpec (eager : Bool) (env : Env) (fe : IFEnv) (f : Nat) :
   113      Prop where
   114    /-- Head normalization without delta, in either mode (`c` is the official
   115    kernel's `cheap_proj`; con-leche's claims generalize the same way). -/
   116    whnfCore : ∀ {c : Bool} (s₀ : AState) (d : Nat) (i : EIdx) (e : Expr),
   117      CheckOK eager env fe s₀ → denoteE s₀.store i = some e →
   118      Expr.WScoped d e →
   119      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ (coreKnot .verified eager fe id f).whnfCore c d i
   120      ⦃fun r s' => CheckOK eager env fe s' ∧ Ext s₀.store s'.store ∧
   121          s'.pins = s₀.pins ∧
   122          SimE (fun F d e => ConLeche.whnfCore .verified eager env F d e c) d e s'.store r; ⊤⦄
   123    /-- The full reduction loop. -/
   124    whnf : ∀ (s₀ : AState) (d : Nat) (i : EIdx) (e : Expr),
   125      CheckOK eager env fe s₀ → denoteE s₀.store i = some e →
   126      Expr.WScoped d e →
   127      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ (coreKnot .verified eager fe id f).whnf d i
   128      ⦃fun r s' => CheckOK eager env fe s' ∧ Ext s₀.store s'.store ∧

    67  theorem knot_spec_all {env : Env} {fe : IFEnv} (henv : ConLeche.EnvWF env) :
    68      ∀ f {eager : Bool}, KnotSpec eager env fe f
    69    | 0, eager => knotSpec_zero eager env fe
    70    | f + 1, _ =>
    71      { whnfCore := fun {c} s₀ d i e hok hden hw =>
    72          memoWhnfCore_step henv
    73            (fun c => whnfCoreBody_spec henv (knot_spec_all henv f) c) (c := c)
    74            s₀ d i e hok hden hw
    75        whnf := fun s₀ d i e hok hden hw =>
    76          memoWhnf_step henv
    77            (whnfBody_spec henv (knot_spec_all henv f)) s₀ d i e hok hden hw
    78        infer := fun s₀ d i e hok hden hw =>
    79          memoInfer_step henv
    80            (inferBody_spec henv (knot_spec_all henv f)) s₀ d i e hok hden hw
    81        defeq := fun s₀ d i j a b hok hda hdb hwa hwb =>
    82          memoDefeq_step henv
    83            (defeqBody_spec henv (knot_spec_all henv f)) s₀ d i j a b hok hda
    84            hdb hwa hwb
    85        defeqE := fun s₀ d i j a b hok hda hdb hwa hwb =>
    86          memoDefeqE_step henv
    87            (defeqBody_spec henv (knot_spec_all henv f)) s₀ d i j a b hok hda
    88            hdb hwa hwb
    89        inferIO := fun s₀ d i e hok hden hw =>
    90          memoInferIO_step henv
    91            (inferBodyIO_spec henv (knot_spec_all henv f)) s₀ d i e hok hden hw }

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L1-L30
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Refine2.Tactic.Lockstep` — the lockstep judgement and the `lockstep` tactic
     3  
     4  Task #97-T2-TACTIC.  Theorem 2 in its lockstep shape (task #97-T2-AUDIT §6)
     5  relates two programs doing the same operations in the same order, over a
     6  state relation that says only "the same data in two representations".  So a
     7  proof of one `_refines` lemma is a ZIP of two do-blocks: peel one bind on each
     8  side, close the correspondence of the two callees with a registered lemma,
     9  continue with the related results.  This file makes that zip a tactic.
    10  
    11  ## The judgement
    12  
    13  `LS pers R m lst x` — *every outcome of the Rust computation `m` is matched by
    14  the twin action `x` run from `lst`*: an `Ok a` by an `ok (b, lst')` with
    15  `R a b` in a related post-state, an `Err e` by the twin throwing at the same
    16  kind (`AErrSim`).  It is `Sim₀` with a relation for the answer instead of an
    17  abstraction function, and with the Rust equation moved into the judgement, so
    18  that the Rust program is visible in the GOAL beside the twin (`LS.toSim₀` is the
    19  bridge back).  Four companion judgements carry the other Rust callee shapes:
    20  
    21  | judgement | Rust callee shape | example |
    22  |---|---|---|
    23  | `LS`  | `Result (Result α CheckError × AState)` — state threaded | `intern_e_app`, a recursive call |
    24  | `LSR` | `Result (Result α CheckError)` — reads, may fail | `view` |
    25  | `LSV` | `Result α` — reads, total | `lift_get`, `inst_list_cutoff` |
    26  | `LSW` | `Result AState` — writes, total | `lift_set` |
    27  | `LSP` | `Result α`, **Rust only** — no twin counterpart | `fuel - 1#u64`, `dup2`, `eidx_nat_key`, `fail` |
    28  | `LSM` | `Result (Result α × AState × M)` — a memoised walk, memo beside the result | `consts_resolve_f_go`, `intern_expr_go` |
    29  | `LSRM` | `Result (Result α × M)` — a memoised reader walk | `all_level_params_defined_go` |
    30  

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L164-L168
   164  /-- **The lockstep judgement** for a state-threading Rust computation. -/
   165  def LS {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   166      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState))
   167      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   168    ∀ o st', m = ok (o, st') → LOut pers R o st' (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L170-L174
   170  /-- A Rust READ that may fail: the state is `st` before and after. -/
   171  def LSR {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   172      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError))
   173      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   174    ∀ o, m = ok o → LOut pers R o st (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L634-L646
   634  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised state walk**: `LS` of the walk with
   635  its memo moved into the answer; `R` relates `(answer, memo)` to the twin's
   636  answer (typically the twin's `(answer, memo)` pair). -/
   637  def LSM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   638      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState × M))
   639      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   640    LS pers R (packM m) lst x
   641  
   642  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised reader walk** at the state `st`. -/
   643  def LSRM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   644      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × M))
   645      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   646    LS pers R (packRM st m) lst x

  2872  /-- **The lockstep tactic**: step until every goal is closed or stuck. -/
  2873  macro "lockstep" : tactic => `(tactic| repeat' lockstep_step)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/ExprOps/Mut.lean#L290-L319
   290  theorem instantiate1_go_aux (n : Nat) :
   291      ∀ {pers : arena.store.PersTier} {st : arena.monad.AState} {lst : AState}
   292        (v : arena.handle.EIdx) (fuel : Std.U64) (h : arena.handle.EIdx) (d : Std.U64),
   293        fuel.val = n → AStateRel₀ pers st lst → AStateInv pers st →
   294        LS pers (fun a b => b = absEIdx a) (arena.expr_ops.instantiate1_go pers st v fuel h d) lst
   295          (instantiate1Go (absEIdx v) n (absEIdx h) (absU d)) := by
   296    induction n with
   297    | zero =>
   298      intro pers st lst v fuel h d hn hrel hinv
   299      rw [arena.expr_ops.instantiate1_go, instantiate1Go_zero]
   300      lockstep
   301    | succ m ih =>
   302      intro pers st lst v fuel h d hn hrel hinv
   303      rw [arena.expr_ops.instantiate1_go, instantiate1Go_succ]
   304      lockstep

   309        (instantiate1Go (absEIdx v) (absU fuel) (absEIdx h) (absU d)) :=
   310    instantiate1_go_aux _ v fuel h d rfl hrel hinv

   614  theorem inst_spine_from_aux (n : Nat) :
   615      ∀ {pers : arena.store.PersTier} {st : arena.monad.AState} {lst : AState}
   616        (fuel : Std.U64) (args : alloc.vec.Vec arena.handle.EIdx) (i : Std.Usize) (t : Std.U64) (e : arena.handle.EIdx),
   617        args.val.length - i.val = n → AStateRel₀ pers st lst → AStateInv pers st →
   618        LS pers (fun a b => b = absEIdx a) (arena.expr_ops.inst_spine_from pers st fuel args i t e) lst
   619          (instSpine (absU fuel) (absEIdxListFrom args i) (absU t) (absEIdx e)) := by
   620    induction n with
   621    | zero =>
   622      intro pers st lst fuel args i t e hn hrel hinv
   623      rw [arena.expr_ops.inst_spine_from, listFrom_nil args i (by omega), instSpine]
   624      lockstep
   625    | succ k ih =>
   626      intro pers st lst fuel args i t e hn hrel hinv
   627      rw [arena.expr_ops.inst_spine_from, listFrom_cons args i (by omega), instSpine]
   628      lockstep

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L18-L137
    18  /-!
    19  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    20  
    21  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    22  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    23  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    24  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's two headline theorems in the shape
    25  the original campaign used (`conron.model_exists` /
    26  `conron.no_False_declaration`, `proof/ConRon/RefineOld/Main.lean`):
    27  
    28  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — every environment the Aeneas model of the
    29    Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    30  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    31    type `False` is never accepted by it.
    32  
    33  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    34  frontier is measured as the dependency closure of these two, and it is
    35  EMPTY since `arena` `db1131f1` (task #97-MILESTONE): both depend on
    36  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` only (§5's census).  What they
    37  still assume is exactly their premises, listed below.
    38  
    39  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    40  
    41  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    42  around six extracted core functions and the pin decoder, in this order, on
    43  one `AState` made from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    44  
    45      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    46        → prepare_prelude → (decode) → intern_all_pins → (the declaration fold)
    47  
    48  The headlines (§4) take one premise per call, from the binary's own start
    49  values `startState`/`emptyTier` (§3); §4's table maps each premise to its line
    50  of `check_main`.
    51  
    52  and the twin runs the same six stages (`Arena/Main.lean`'s
    53  `runPipelineHead`/`runPipelineTail` drive them for `con-ron-lean`).  **The sixth stage is the fold the
    54  binary's driver runs, pool and all** (task #97-P5-POOL):
    55  `driver::check_decls_driver` runs phase A with the heartbeat as its hook,
    56  freezes the tier, runs phase B on `pool::parallel_all`, and thaws the tier.
    57  The headlines take one premise per step (`h6` phase A, `hord` the jobs' order, `h7` the
    58  freeze, `hlayer` the value checks' layer, `h8` phase B), which `poolAccepts_intro` assembles
    59  into `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  Phase B's premise `h8` is the contract
    60  of the generic combinator `pool::parallel_all` with the driver's two verified closures
    61  (`ParallelAll` at `jobStep`): index lists, one per worker, covering every job, and for each
    62  a fold of `run_job` over its indices from `worker_state`, accepting.  That contract is the
    63  pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.
    64  The theorems hold for EVERY install hook, so they cover the plain run and
    65  `--progress` alike.  `pool_accepts_refines` relates the stage to the twin's
    66  `Arena.PooledAccepts`, and `Bridge/Checker/Phased.lean`'s
    67  `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` carries that to the pure fold.  So the
    68  statement takes the six Rust RUNS as premises (that the binary's
    69  `check_main` makes exactly these calls, in this order, is the one trusted
    70  line, exactly as it was for the original campaign), and the proof is:
    71  
    72  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s six `…_refines` lemmas walk the
    73     Rust runs into six TWIN runs from the twin's own start state
    74     `AState.init EStore.empty`, related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/
    75     `AStateInv`: lockstep);
    76  2. **Theorem 1** — the twin runs feed `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`, whose
    77     pure fold accepts the denoted stream: con-leche's
    78     `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` gives the model, and
    79     `no_False_theorem_accepted_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream
    80     (`stages_no_False`, through the pure fold);
    81  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a
    82     model.
    83  
    84  Every step is an existing theorem; what this file adds is glue: the Rust
    85  runs threaded through `Sim₀`/`SimStream`/`SimFold`, and the one twin-store
    86  fact the composition needs from Theorem 1 — `StoreWF` at the headline's
    87  `AStateRel` (`stages_storeWF`) — read off its stage lemmas.  Theorem 2 itself
    88  carries no fact about the twin's store (task #97-T2-AUDIT).
    89  
    90  ## The named hypotheses
    91  
    92  Since task #98-HEADLINE the headlines start from the binary's own start
    93  values (`startState` = `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`)
    94  instead of quantifying over a start state with `hpers`/`hest`/`hst0`
    95  equations, name the call the binary makes at each step (`prepare_d`, not
    96  `prepare_prelude`).  Beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape
    97  `hfalse` and the one premise per call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`, `hord`, `hlayer`), what
    98  they assume is exactly:
    99  
   100  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks
   101    (task #97-P5-Driver): the binary parses with the verified reader loop
   102    `parse_source` over the driver's file handle, and
   103    `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that
   104    `parse_chunks` over the chunks the handle hands out; that the handle hands
   105    out the file's bytes, in order, is the input seam — the one seam left.
   106  
   107  Former hypotheses, now theorems or gone (DESIGN.md's task #97-COMPOSE and
   108  #98-HEADLINE sections tag each with its owning lane):
   109  
   110  * ~~`InitRel`~~ — the Rust start state is related to the twin's: a theorem

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L1-L55
     1  //! `driver` — con-leche's `Driver/{Cli,CheckMain,Run}.lean`, over the ARENA (tasks #37, #48 and
     2  //! #97-P4f), and the Rust side of the Lean twin's
     3  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Main.lean`.
     4  //!
     5  //! The module is that driver in its order: the reads,
     6  //! the two phases with the boundary visible, the `--progress` heartbeat behind
     7  //! one observer trait, the verdict lines, the exit-code mapping, and the flag
     8  //! parsers.  Task #97-SWAP put it here, under the name the shipping driver
     9  //! always had: it was `crates/con-ron-arena/src/driver.rs` through the arena
    10  //! campaign, beside the `Expr`-tree driver it has now replaced, and the
    11  //! eleven representation-free items it used to import across the crate line
    12  //! ([`exit_code`], `verdict_word`, `message`, `ms_secs`, `progress_stride`,
    13  //! `jobs_count`, `default_jobs`, [`workers_for`],
    14  //! `read_up_to`, `STACK_BYTES`) are back in it, unchanged.
    15  //!
    16  //! ## THE EXIT CODES
    17  //!
    18  //! | exit | verdict | meaning |
    19  //! |---|---|---|
    20  //! | 0 | `accepted N declarations` | every declaration checked; `N` counts the file's declaration records |
    21  //! | 1 | `rejected` | a declaration is invalid |
    22  //! | 2 | `declined` | the checker positively detected a feature it does not support, and says which |
    23  //! | 3 | error | bad usage, malformed input, or an internal failure of unclear cause |
    24  //!
    25  //! ## What the arena changed about the driver
    26  //!
    27  //! 1. **The state is one `AState`** (`con_ron_core::arena::monad::AState`: the
    28  //!    store, the per-call memos, the per-declaration caches), threaded as a
    29  //!    `&mut` through the parse, the preparation, the pin walk and both phases.
    30  //!    The `Expr`-tree driver threaded a `CState` and the declarations carried
    31  //!    their own terms; here the terms are in the state and the records are
    32  //!    handles into it, so nothing may be run against a state that is not the
    33  //!    one they were interned into.
    34  //! 2. **`intern_all_pins` runs once, before the fold, with the scratch tier
    35  //!    off** (DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d, task #97-P4d's "for P4f"): every pinned datum
    36  //!    is in the PERSISTENT cons table before any declaration's check can
    37  //!    intern one into a tier that is about to vanish.  Its result — the
    38  //!    interned pin list — is the fold's parameter.
    39  //! 3. **Phase B's bracket is `run_job`'s** (`check_pending`'s and
    40  //!    `block_check`'s), which empties the scratch tier around each job.  A
    41  //!    driver that checked records itself without it would grow the scratch tier
    42  //!    without bound; the pool calls it once per job and nothing else opens a
    43  //!    tier.
    44  //! 4. **Phase B runs on [`crate::pool`] at every `--jobs=<n>`**, which is
    45  //!    DESIGN.md §8.3's arrangement and needs no atomics: the persistent tier
    46  //!    and the installed index are immutable in phase B, so they are shared by
    47  //!    reference, and each worker owns a scratch tier, its own caches and a copy
    48  //!    of the pin handles.  `--jobs=1` is the same install and the same jobs on
    49  //!    one worker.
    50  //!
    51  //! ## The read loop
    52  //!
    53  //! [`parse_export_handle_d`] is `ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean`'s
    54  //! `foldChunks` over forward reads (its positional reads and its parallel
    55  //! rounds parse are not ported): the VERIFIED loop `export_c::parse_source` (task

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L548-L648
   548  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:317-334 checkDecls
   549  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/Run.lean:50-210 checkDeclsIO
   550  /// **The driver**: the two-phase fold with the boundary visible — a straight
   551  /// line of calls, with the observer's lines between them and the pool for
   552  /// phase B, at every job count.  Each step is one premise of the capstone:
   553  ///
   554  /// | step | here | the capstone's premise |
   555  /// |---|---|---|
   556  /// | phase A | `checker::install_fold_hooked(…, fold_start(), ds, 0, obs)` | the same call accepts |
   557  /// | boundary | `checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store, fe)` | the same call's value |
   558  /// | phase B | `pool::parallel_all(m, workers, ‖ worker_state(pins), ‖w, k‖ run_job(&tier, w, mode, &layer, &pend, &blocks, &order[k]), …)` | `h8`: index lists `ws` covering `0..order.len`, each `w` a `foldlM` of `run_job` over `k ∈ w` from `worker_state pins`, accepting (internally `ParallelAll`) |
   559  /// | after | `checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier)` | restores the store and hands `fe` back (`freeze_tier_ok`) |
   560  ///
   561  /// `init` and `step` are calls into the verified crate; `parallel_all` is the
   562  /// one trusted piece, and its contract (`pool.rs`'s note) is exactly
   563  /// `ParallelAll`: on `Ok`, every job was run by some worker, each worker folding
   564  /// `run_job` over the jobs it claimed on ONE `worker_state`.  Everything else
   565  /// here is the observer, which only ever holds `&` the state (the hook of phase
   566  /// A by the trait's own signature, the other lines through `&st.store` and the
   567  /// worker's `&AState`), so it cannot change an outcome.
   568  ///
   569  /// **Phase A failing** runs the block jobs before it (`checker::phase_a_failure`):
   570  /// a stored block is checked only by its job, and a failure past it may be that
   571  /// block's doing, so the verdict is the first failing job's.  **Phase B** merges
   572  /// the value checks and the block jobs in fold order (`checker::job_order`), and
   573  /// the pool reports the least failing index, so the first failure in fold order
   574  /// is the verdict at every job count.
   575  ///
   576  /// **The boundary is where the tier is FROZEN.**  Phase A owns its persistent
   577  /// tier and its index and appends to them; at the boundary `checker::freeze_tier`
   578  /// moves the four stores' persistent tables and the index into one `PersTier`,
   579  /// handed back `frozen`: every read through it goes to those tables, and a
   580  /// worker's own store is frozen (`checker::worker_state`), so every append there
   581  /// is a scratch append.  So `n` workers share one environment and one term DAG and
   582  /// own nothing but a scratch tier, their caches and a copy of the pin handles.
   583  pub fn check_decls_driver<O: PhaseObserver + InstallHook + Send>(
   584      pers: &PersTier,
   585      st: &mut AState,
   586      mode: &CheckMode,
   587      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   588      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   589      jobs: u64,
   590      obs: &mut O,
   591  ) -> Result<IFEnv, (CheckError, u64)> {
   592      let total = ds.len();
   593      // PHASE A (ConRon.Capstone: h6): the verified fold, the heartbeat as hook.
   594      let p = match checker::install_fold_hooked(pers, st, mode, pins, checker::fold_start(), ds, 0, &*obs) {
   595          Err((e, i)) => {
   596              let f = checker::phase_a_failure(pers, st, mode, pins, ds, e, i);
   597              obs.install_failed(f.1, total);
   598              return Err(f);
   599          }
   600          Ok(p) => p,
   601      };
   602      let (_n_installed, fe, pend, blocks): (u64, IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>, Vec<BlockCheck>) = p;
   603      let order: Vec<(bool, u64)> = checker::job_order(&pend, &blocks);  // ConRon.Capstone: hord
   604      let m = order.len();
   605      obs.install_done(pers, &st.store, total, m, blocks.len());
   606      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   607      obs.phase_b_workers(workers);
   608      // THE PHASE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier and the index leave the state and
   609      // become a value every worker reads (the doc comment above).  `st` keeps its
   610      // (empty) store, its tables moved out, so the observer can still read a
   611      // label back through the tier.  (ConRon.Capstone: h7)
   612      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store, fe);
   613      let layer: IFEnv = checker::check_layer();  // ConRon.Capstone: hlayer
   614      // PHASE B: `run_job` at every job, on `workers` threads, each folding it over
   615      // the jobs it claims on ONE `worker_state` — the verdict and the record a
   616      // rejection names are the one-worker walk's at every `--jobs` (the least
   617      // failing index).  (ConRon.Capstone: h8)
   618      let heartbeat = obs.wants_check_lines();
   619      let lock: Mutex<(usize, &mut O)> = Mutex::new((0, obs));
   620      let r = parallel_all(
   621          m,
   622          workers,
   623          || checker::worker_state(&st.pins),
   624          |w: &mut AState, k| checker::run_job(&tier, w, mode, &layer, &pend, &blocks, &order[k]),
   625          |w: &AState, k| check_line(heartbeat, &lock, &tier, w, m, &job_at(&order, &pend, &blocks, k)),
   626      );
   627      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   628          Ok((_, o)) => o,
   629          Err(e) => e.into_inner().1,
   630      };
   631      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the fold — the verdict line's
   632      // declaration label, the failing record's name, the receipts — reads a
   633      // handle back out of `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has
   634      // gone out of scope answers `None` to every one of them (the first
   635      // version of this printed `at theorem ?` where the tip printed `at
   636      // theorem addOk`).  `thaw_tier` is `freeze_tier` inverted.
   637      let fe: IFEnv = checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   638      match phase_b_verdict(&order, &pend, &blocks, r) {
   639          Err((e, pos)) => {
   640              obs.check_failed(pos);
   641              Err((e, pos))
   642          }
   643          Ok(()) => {
   644              obs.check_done(m);
   645              Ok(fe)
   646          }
   647      }
   648  }

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L45-L97
    45  //! ## THE TRUSTED CLAIM, and the whole of it
    46  //!
    47  //! **If `parallel_all(n, workers, init, step, after)` returns `Ok(())`, then
    48  //! every index in `0..n` was claimed by some worker; each worker built its
    49  //! state with `init()` exactly once and folded `step` over the indices it
    50  //! claimed, in claim order; and every one of those `step` calls returned
    51  //! `Ok(())`** — at every worker count.  That is `ParallelAll` in
    52  //! `proof/ConRon/Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean` (task #98-POOL), and it is a
    53  //! statement about this module's control flow only — nothing about what
    54  //! `init` and `step` compute.  With the driver's closures it is the
    55  //! capstone's pool premise `h8` (task #98-H8 states it inline: index lists
    56  //! `ws` covering `0..order.len`, and for each `w` in `ws` a `foldlM` of
    57  //! `run_job` over `w` from `worker_state pins`, accepting), which the
    58  //! proof relates, worker by worker, to the twin (`PoolAccepts.toParts`,
    59  //! `pool_accepts_refines`).
    60  //!
    61  //! The claim is deliberately weaker than what the code does (task #98-H8):
    62  //! the counter below hands each index to exactly ONE worker and a worker's
    63  //! claims INCREASE, but the contract promises neither — the proof needs only
    64  //! coverage, since each job reads only its own prefix environment and the
    65  //! twin's grouping theorem holds for any order, any split and any repetition.
    66  //! The argument:
    67  //!
    68  //! * **A claim is a `fetch_add` on one counter.**  Each value `0, 1, 2, …` is
    69  //!   handed to exactly one caller, so every index in `0..n` is claimed (by
    70  //!   exactly one worker, in fact).  A worker stops at its first claim `≥ n`.
    71  //! * **A worker is one fold.**  `worker` calls `init()` once, then for each
    72  //!   claimed index `k` calls `step(&mut st, k)` on that one state — the fold,
    73  //!   in claim order.  `after(&st, k)` sees the state by `&` only.  A claimed
    74  //!   index at or above `limit` is skipped without a call, and on an accepting
    75  //!   run the limit never moves (only a failing step lowers it), so no claimed
    76  //!   index is skipped.
    77  //! * **Merge by index — master's argument.**  A worker hands back each index
    78  //!   it stepped with the step's result; the workers' arrays are merged *by
    79  //!   index* into one table and `first_failure` walks it in index order,
    80  //!   answering `Ok` only if every slot holds `Ok`.  So an accept means every
    81  //!   index was stepped, successfully, by the worker that claimed it, whatever
    82  //!   the timing.  An empty slot is `ParallelError::Missing`, never `Ok`.
    83  //!
    84  //! The failure side is not part of the claim the capstone uses, but the pool
    85  //! keeps master's behaviour there: the walk stops at the first failing index,
    86  //! and the table is complete below it.  con-leche's argument: a worker whose
    87  //! step fails at `f` lowers the shared `limit` to `f`, and a worker skips a
    88  //! claimed index at or above the limit.  Every value the limit ever holds is
    89  //! `n` or a *failing* index, hence at least the first failing index `f`; so an
    90  //! index below `f` is never skipped, and — the counter being monotone — it was
    91  //! claimed before `f` was and is finished by the worker that claimed it.
    92  //! `pool_reports_the_first_failure_at_every_jobs` is the test, at 1, 2, 3, 4
    93  //! and 8 workers on a list whose records 2 and 4 both fail;
    94  //! `pool_is_the_one_worker_walk_at_every_jobs` checks that phase B's verdict
    95  //! is the one-worker walk's; `parallel_all_partitions_the_indices` checks the
    96  //! claim itself on a state that records its claims.
    97  //!

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean#L307-L311
   307  def ParallelAll {S E : Type} (n : Nat) (init : Result S)
   308      (step : S → Nat → Result (core.result.Result Unit E × S)) : Prop :=
   309    ∃ parts : List (List Nat),
   310      (∀ k < n, ∃ w ∈ parts, k ∈ w) ∧
   311      ∀ w ∈ parts, ∃ s₀, init = ok s₀ ∧ FoldAllOk step s₀ w

     6  # Runs, in order, and stops at the first failure:
     7  #   1. cargo build                          the crate compiles, warning-free
     8  #   2. cargo test                           the unit tests pass
     9  #   3. scripts/lint-rust-style.sh           the Aeneas subset (§3.4), both crates
    10  #      scripts/dead-rust.py --check         no `pub` Rust item without a caller
    11  #                                           (task #105)
    12  #   4. scripts/provenance.py check          every item cites con-leche (§3.7)
    13  #      scripts/pin-last.py                  no commit but the tip moves the
    14  #                                           con-leche pin (§7, task #108)
    15  #   5. scripts/provenance-selftest.py        the gate's Lean parser and the
    16  #                                           bump classifier, on their fixtures
    17  #   6. scripts/twin-lines.py check          every `Lean twin:` line names a
    18  #                                           declaration of `proof/ConRon/**` at
    19  #                                           its current lines (§3.7)
    20  #   7. scripts/overview-links.sh            OVERVIEW.md/DESIGN.md line anchors
    21  #   8. scripts/holes.sh --check             OVERVIEW.md §8.1 == the model's holes
    22  #   9. scripts/gen-pins.sh --check          embedded pin text == natOpPinSets
    23  #  10. scripts/gen-prelude.sh --check       embedded prelude text == con-leche's
    24  #  11. scripts/gen-prelude-lean.sh --check  (B)'s embedded prelude bytes, ditto
    25  #  12. scripts/extract.sh --check           committed generated Lean == crate
    26  #  13. cd proof && lake build               the default targets elaborate: every
    27  #                                           library of the chain, Theorem 1
    28  #                                           (`ConRonBridge`), Theorem 2
    29  #                                           (`ConRonRefine2`), the composition
    30  #                                           (`ConRonCapstone`) included; any
    31  #      warning from proof/'s own sources fails it (lake-build-wfail.sh, #102)

    33  #      has no jobs flag; the first con-leche build can exhaust memory, #74)

    35  #                                           unreachable from the headline
    36  #                                           theorems, Tests and tooling (#105)
